# SOP-INC-001 - Rental income

> **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT.** Authored for a technical assessment. This is not an
> IRAS document and does not reflect IRAS internal material, templates or
> practice. Every factual claim is a restatement traceable to the public
> source cited beside it in section 2.

> **HELD OUT OF THE INDEX.** This procedure is authored but excluded from
> the runtime lookup, so the classes it serves resolve to no SOP. See
> `sop_design.md` S5.

## 1. Scope

Taxpayer asks whether rent received is taxable, when rental income must be declared, what expenses may be deducted, or how the simplified claim for rental expenses works.

**Not in scope:**
- The taxpayer's own declared rental figures or assessment. -> escalate (`account_specific`)
- Computing net rental income or tax for the taxpayer. -> escalate (`amount_computation_requested`)
- Property tax, which is a different tax type. -> escalate (`oos_other_agency`)

## 2. Key facts the officer may state

- Rent payments received from renting out a property are subject to income tax and must be declared in the Income Tax Return.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- Net rental income, after deduction of allowable expenses, is subject to income tax.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- Rental income is taxable from the date it is due and payable to the property owner, not the date it is actually received. Rent due in 2025 but paid in 2026 is declared for Year of Assessment 2026.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- Any amount recovered from insurance on a property that is rented out is taxable and should be reported as part of income.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- Under the simplified claim for rental expenses for tenanted residential property, deemed rental expenses calculated as 15% of gross rent are pre-filled in the online tax form.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- In addition to the 15% deemed rental expenses, property owners may still claim mortgage interest on the loan taken to purchase the property.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- The amount of taxable rental income depends on whether the property is solely or jointly owned.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>

## 3. Decision steps

1. **If** Asking about their own declared rental figures or assessment  
   -> Escalate (`account_specific`)
2. **If** Asking IRAS to compute net rental income or tax  
   -> Escalate (`amount_computation_requested`)
3. **If** Asking about property tax rather than income tax on rent  
   -> Redirect (`oos_other_agency`)
4. **If** Otherwise  
   -> State the treatment of rental income from the key facts

## 4. Approved phrasing

**`taxable`**

> Rent you receive from renting out your property is subject to income tax and must be declared in your Income Tax Return. It is the net rental income, after deducting allowable expenses, that is taxed.

**`timing`**

> Rental income is taxable from the date it is due and payable to you, rather than the date you actually receive it. For example, rent due to you in 2025 but paid in January 2026 is declared for Year of Assessment 2026.

**`simplified_expenses`**

> For tenanted residential property, a simplified claim is available: deemed rental expenses of 15% of your gross rent are pre-filled in the online tax form. You may still claim mortgage interest on the loan taken to purchase the property in addition to the 15%.

## 5. Do not

- Do not compute net rental income, allowable expenses or tax payable.
- Do not confirm a taxpayer's own declared figures.
- Do not advise whether the simplified claim or actual expenses is more advantageous for a particular taxpayer.
- Do not answer property tax questions from this procedure.

## 6. Related

- SOP-FIL-001
- SOP-RTE-002

# SOP-REL-005 - Personal income tax relief cap

> **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT.** Authored for a technical assessment. This is not an
> IRAS document and does not reflect IRAS internal material, templates or
> practice. Every factual claim is a restatement traceable to the public
> source cited beside it in section 2.

> **HELD OUT OF THE INDEX.** This procedure is authored but excluded from
> the runtime lookup, so the classes it serves resolve to no SOP. See
> `sop_design.md` S5.

## 1. Scope

Taxpayer asks whether there is a limit on the total amount of personal reliefs they may claim, how the cap applies across different reliefs, or what happens when their claims exceed it.

**Not in scope:**
- Whether this taxpayer's own reliefs exceed the cap, and by how much. -> escalate (`account_specific`)
- Computing the taxpayer's total reliefs or resulting tax. -> escalate (`amount_computation_requested`)

## 2. Key facts the officer may state

- A personal income tax relief cap of $80,000 applies to the total amount of all tax reliefs claimed for each Year of Assessment.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- A taxpayer is affected by the cap if the total amount of personal reliefs they claim exceeds $80,000.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- The overall personal income tax relief cap takes effect from Year of Assessment 2018.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- The cap applies to the total of all personal reliefs taken together. It is not a limit within any single relief, so it cannot be determined from the rules of one relief alone.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- Where the cap applies, the reliefs allowed are limited to $80,000, and this is reflected in the Notice of Assessment.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- The cap applies to the total of all reliefs, including relief on compulsory and voluntary CPF contributions.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- The $80,000 cap operates on top of the individual caps within specific reliefs, such as the $50,000 per-child cap on QCR or Child Relief (Disability) combined with WMCR.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/working-mother's-child-relief-(wmcr)</sup>
- There is no refund of accepted voluntary CPF or SRS contributions where the relief cap means they attract no tax relief.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>

## 3. Decision steps

1. **If** Asking whether their own reliefs exceed the cap  
   -> Escalate (`account_specific`)
2. **If** Asking IRAS to total their reliefs or compute the effect of the cap  
   -> Escalate (`amount_computation_requested`)
3. **If** Otherwise  
   -> State the cap and how it applies from the key facts

## 4. Approved phrasing

**`cap`**

> A personal income tax relief cap of $80,000 applies to the total amount of all tax reliefs you claim in each Year of Assessment. If the total of your personal reliefs exceeds $80,000, the reliefs allowed to you are limited to $80,000, and this is reflected in your Notice of Assessment.

**`interaction`**

> The $80,000 cap applies on top of the caps within individual reliefs, such as the $50,000 combined cap per child on Qualifying Child Relief and Working Mother's Child Relief.

**`no_refund`**

> Please note that voluntary CPF and SRS contributions cannot be refunded if the relief cap means they do not attract tax relief, so it is worth considering the cap before making a voluntary contribution.

## 5. Do not

- Do not total a taxpayer's reliefs or compute the effect of the cap for them.
- Do not confirm whether a specific taxpayer is affected by the cap.
- Do not advise whether a voluntary contribution is financially worthwhile.

## 6. Related

- SOP-REL-001
- SOP-REL-002
- SOP-REL-003
- SOP-REL-004

# Data sources, licensing, and privacy

Every input to this project, where it came from, what licence governs it, and what
was done to it. Nothing in `data/` is real citizen correspondence.

---

## 1. Summary

| Asset | Origin | Committed? | Licence position |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data/sop/*.md` — 17 SOPs | **Authored by me**, facts traced to public IRAS pages | Yes | Original work. Facts are not copyrightable. |
| `data/scenarios/*.yaml` — 116 situations | **Authored by me** | Yes | Original work. |
| `data/generated/emails.jsonl` — 3,000 emails | Generated by GPT-4o from the scenario specs | Yes | Model output; OpenAI grants output rights to the caller. |
| `data/splits/splits.json` | Derived, seeded | Yes | Derived artefact. |
| IRAS guidance pages (30 URLs) | `iras.gov.sg` | **No — gitignored** | Read as reference only. Not redistributed. |
| CFPB Consumer Complaint Database | Accessed through Hugging Face | **No** | Read for register/style only; no complaint text is retained, redistributed, or used for training/evaluation. |
| `models/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` | Hugging Face | Yes | Apache 2.0; upstream licence and attribution are included beside the weights. |

---

## 2. The SOP corpus — authored, not scraped

**No agency publishes its internal SOPs.** Any honest version of this project must
author them, and pretending otherwise would be the more serious misrepresentation.

Each of the 17 SOPs is a **synthetic officer-facing procedure**. Every factual claim
in one traces to a public IRAS URL recorded in that file's `references:` frontmatter —
**30 distinct URLs**, all on `www.iras.gov.sg`.

Three structural guarantees, enforced at load time rather than by convention:

- **Every SOP carries a synthetic banner.** `src/triage/sop/loader.py` raises at
  startup if `synthetic: true` is missing. A corpus that could be mistaken for real
  agency material is the failure mode this guards against.
- **Every SOP must declare at least one reference.** An empty `references:` list is a
  hard load error.
- **Citations are checked, not assumed.** `python scripts/generate_sops.py --check`
  validates that all 148 recorded facts resolve to a declared source. It is a
  Makefile target and part of the normal build.

None of these files reflects internal IRAS material, template, or practice. They are
my reconstruction of what such a procedure would plausibly contain. The
[SOP authoring schema](sop_specs/README.md) is the integration point through which a
real agency could provide its own procedures without changing application code.

### 2.1 How the reference pages were used

`scripts/fetch_reference.py` fetches the registry of public pages into `.scratch/`,
which is **gitignored** (`.gitignore` line 3). The manifest records the URL, fetch date
(2026-09-01), HTTP status and byte count for each.

The fetched HTML exists **only** so that facts written into the SOP specs can be
checked against their source during human review. It is never committed, never
redistributed, and never fed to a model.

Politeness measures: a courtesy rate-limit between requests (`--delay`, default
applied in the fetch loop), a single pass rather than a crawl, and a fixed registry of
~30 named pages rather than link-following. A browser User-Agent is set because the
IRAS site serves a JavaScript navigation shell to unknown agents and returns no
content otherwise — this is to receive the page a human would see, not to evade a
restriction.

`https://www.iras.gov.sg/robots.txt` was checked on **2026-09-03** and returned HTTP
404, so there were no published crawler directives to apply. Absence of a robots file
is not treated as permission: the fixed allowlist, one-second delay, single pass, and
Terms-of-Use analysis below still govern the fetch.

### 2.2 Licensing position, stated plainly

IRAS Terms of Use restrict reproduction of site contents. Read literally, they also
require written permission to hyperlink to an internal page — a provision that reads
as boilerplate and is not observed in practice anywhere on the Singapore web.

**This project does not depend on resolving that question**, because it does not
reproduce site content. The operative principle is that **copyright protects
expression, not facts**. A filing deadline, a relief cap, and a penalty rate are facts
stated in or derived from legislation; they are not anyone's creative expression.

What is committed is my own prose restating those facts, with a citation to where each
came from. What is not committed is any IRAS page, in whole or in part.

**Note on figures.** Relief caps and rates in the SOPs are stated as the public pages
state them. They are a snapshot taken 2026-09-01 and will go stale — a production
version would need effective-date metadata and a re-indexing cadence, which is listed
under future improvements in the README.

---

## 3. Synthetic emails

3,000 emails generated by **GPT-4o** from 116 hand-authored scenario specifications.

### 3.1 Why synthetic

Real citizen correspondence to a tax authority contains NRICs, addresses, income
figures and financial distress. It cannot be obtained lawfully for a take-home
exercise, cannot be ethically used if it could, and no public corpus of Singapore
government email enquiries exists. Synthetic is the only honest option here, and the
question becomes whether it is generated well enough to support a claim.

### 3.2 What makes it defensible

**The generator never sees the label.** It receives a *situation* description
("someone received a message claiming to be from the tax authority asking them to
confirm bank details, and wants to know if it is real"). The class label is attached
afterward from the scenario file. The model cannot write toward a class name, which is
the mechanism that would otherwise plant a giveaway token in every email of a class.

**Three independent axes of variation:**

- *Content* — persona, life situation, and the guidance actually relevant to it.
- *Style* — standard English; imperfect English with typos, run-ons and all-caps;
  lightly Singlish-inflected. Register calibrated against sampled real CFPB complaints
  (read for tone; no text copied).
- *Season* — filing period, estimates, notice-of-assessment period.

Plus an edge-case slice: answerable only from held-out guidance, account-specific
phrasing, and genuine edge cases recalled from prior call-centre experience.

**Model separation.** The generator (OpenAI GPT-4o) differs from the zero-shot
classification baseline and the groundedness judge (both Groq/Qwen). No model in the
evaluation path is ever scored on text it wrote — enforced as an explicit rule in
`config/models.yaml`.

### 3.3 Leakage is tested, not assumed

`python scripts/check_leakage.py` runs seven checks over the committed corpus. All
seven pass on the current one:

0. **Balance** — class counts against the taxonomy (300 per class × 10).
1. **Vocabulary leakage** — a TF-IDF + logistic-regression probe. It should classify
   *well but not perfectly*: a near-perfect score means a giveaway token exists and the
   corpus needs regenerating. Measured accuracy sits in the expected band.
2. **System vocabulary** — no email contains the system's own terms (bucket names,
   SOP ids, class names).
3. **Length as a giveaway** — that message length alone does not carry class signal.
4. **Near-duplicates** — cosine similarity across the corpus.
5. **Boilerplate** — that generated openings and closings do not cluster by class.
6. **Flag confounding** — that a lexical flag is not standing in for a class.

Separately, **splits are grouped by `scenario_id`**, so every variant of a situation
lands in the same split and no paraphrase straddles the train/test boundary. That is
enforced in `scripts/make_splits.py` and verified by zero scenario overlap between
every pair of splits.

### 3.4 Privacy in the generated data

- **All identifiers were generated for the project, not sourced from people.** NRICs
  are checksum-valid so the detector can be tested honestly. The values were not
  checked against official registries, so accidental collision cannot be ruled out.
- Addresses combine public Singapore street and estate names with generated block and
  unit numbers. Phone numbers and postal codes are generated in valid-looking shapes.
- No personal identifier belonging to the author or a known person was used.
- **What was planted is recorded** (`plant_pii` per email), which is what makes scrub
  recall measurable rather than asserted.

### 3.5 Privacy in the pipeline itself

Beyond the data, three properties of the system:

- **Scrubbing happens before any external call.** The classifier and the drafter both
  see placeholder text; real values never leave the machine. Rehydration is local and
  happens after the network call, in exactly one place.
- **No PII in committed results.** `eval/metrics/pii_recall.py` masks missed values at
  the point of capture (`S0433218J` → `S0*****8J`), so the module that measures
  containment cannot itself write an identifier into `eval/results/`.
- **`.env` is gitignored** and `triage.env.key_status()` reports only booleans, never
  key values.

---

## 4. CFPB Consumer Complaint Database

- **Source:** [US Consumer Financial Protection Bureau complaint
  database](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/data-research/consumer-complaints/),
  accessed through a Hugging Face copy during style review.
- **Privacy:** CFPB publishes complaint narratives only after removing personal
  information. No narrative is stored or redistributed by this project.
- **Use:** read to calibrate *register* — how members of the public actually write to
  an institution when frustrated, confused, or in financial difficulty. Sentence
  length, politeness markers, how a complaint opens.
- **Not used for:** training, evaluation, or text reuse. No CFPB text appears in this
  repository. It is American and about consumer finance, so it is a style reference
  only, never a content one.

---

## 5. Model weights

- **`sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`** — Apache 2.0, from Hugging Face.
  Committed to the repo (~88 MB fine-tuned) so a clone yields real weights rather than
  git-lfs pointers. The upstream licence and attribution notice are included beside
  both the base encoder and the fine-tuned derivative.
- Gemini, Groq and OpenAI are accessed by API under their respective terms. No weights
  are redistributed.

---

## 6. What this data does not cover

Recorded here as well as in the README, because it bounds every number reported:

- **116 situations is the binding constraint**, not 3,000 emails. Per-class figures
  rest on ~90 test emails drawn from a handful of situations each, so a class can look
  strong because its few situations happen to be easy.
- **A synthetic ceiling.** This measures performance on a distribution GPT-4o and I
  jointly imagined. It cannot tell you a real inbox looks like this — that is the one
  thing this project cannot check about itself.
- **One agency, one tax type.** Individual income tax only. No corporate tax, GST,
  property tax, or stamp duty.
- **English only**, with Singlish inflection. No Chinese, Malay or Tamil.
- **No attachments, no threads, no forwarded chains.** Every email is a single
  standalone message, which real correspondence often is not.
- **Author-shaped distribution.** The scenario set reflects what I judged
  representative. A real inbox would be shaped by seasonality, campaigns, and
  events nobody anticipated.

The most valuable next data step is not more emails — it is **more situations**, and a
validation-only slice of real anonymised enquiries to test whether the synthetic
situation set resembles the real one.

# SOP-PAY-001 - Handling GIRO enquiries

> **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT.** Authored for a technical assessment. This is not an
> IRAS document and does not reflect IRAS internal material, templates or
> practice. Every factual claim is a restatement traceable to the public
> source cited beside it in section 2.

## 1. Scope

Taxpayer asks how GIRO works, how to apply, when deductions occur, what happens when a deduction fails, how the provisional instalment plan works, or how to edit, cancel or re-activate an arrangement.

**Not in scope:**
- The status of a specific taxpayer's GIRO plan, or why their deduction failed. -> escalate (`account_specific`)
- Restructuring instalments because the taxpayer cannot afford them. -> escalate (`hardship_or_waiver_request`)
- Computing an instalment amount for a specific taxpayer. -> escalate (`amount_computation_requested`)

## 2. Key facts the officer may state

- Tax may be paid by GIRO either in monthly instalments of up to 12 months, or as a one-time yearly payment.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- Monthly GIRO deductions are made on the 6th of each month.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- If the deduction date falls on a weekend or public holiday, the deduction is made on the next working day.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- If a GIRO deduction is unsuccessful, a second deduction is attempted on the 20th of the month.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- A GIRO arrangement is cancelled after 2 consecutive months of failed deductions, that is, 4 failed deductions in a row.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- The Provisional Instalment Plan (PIP) commences yearly from May, based on the previous year's tax or the current year's estimated tax payable.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- Once the assessment is finalised, the monthly GIRO arrangement is revised based on the actual tax payable.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- Where a taxpayer joins GIRO after May, instalment deductions commence in the month after the application is approved and end in April of the following year.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- eGIRO applications may be made through myTax Portal (set up within minutes), through the DBS/POSB, OCBC or UOB bank portals (within 3 working days), or at AXS stations (within 3 working days).  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- Hard copy GIRO applications require up to 21 working days to process, and the exact timeline is subject to the respective bank's processing.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- GIRO must be applied for using an SGD savings or current account with a participating bank.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- For a successful deduction the account must hold sufficient funds on the deduction date and have a suitable payment limit set. Some banks may impose charges for unsuccessful GIRO deductions.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- A cancelled GIRO arrangement may be re-activated through the 'Apply/Manage GIRO Plan' digital service at myTax Portal.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- To terminate a GIRO arrangement entirely, the taxpayer must contact their bank directly; a cancelled arrangement can still be re-activated with IRAS.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>

## 3. Decision steps

1. **If** Asking about their own plan, a specific failed deduction, or their own instalment amount  
   -> Escalate (`account_specific`)
2. **If** Requesting penalty waiver, or restructuring because they cannot afford the instalments  
   -> Escalate (`hardship_or_waiver_request`)
3. **If** Asking IRAS to calculate an instalment amount or a balance  
   -> Escalate (`amount_computation_requested`)
4. **If** Otherwise  
   -> Answer from the key facts and direct to the application channels

## 4. Approved phrasing

**`giro_dates`**

> Payments by GIRO are deducted on the 6th of each month. If the 6th falls on a weekend or public holiday, the deduction is made on the next working day. Where a deduction is unsuccessful, a second attempt is made on the 20th of the month.

**`giro_failure`**

> A GIRO arrangement is cancelled after two consecutive months of failed deductions, that is, four failed deductions in a row. Please ensure that your account holds sufficient funds on the deduction date and that a suitable payment limit is set. If your arrangement has been cancelled, you may re-activate it through the 'Apply/Manage GIRO Plan' digital service at myTax Portal.

**`giro_apply`**

> You can apply for eGIRO through myTax Portal, which is set up within minutes, or through the DBS/POSB, OCBC and UOB bank portals and AXS stations, which take up to 3 working days. GIRO must be set up using an SGD savings or current account with a participating bank.

**`pip`**

> The Provisional Instalment Plan begins in May each year and is based on the previous year's tax or the current year's estimated tax payable. Once your assessment is finalised, your monthly instalments are revised to reflect the actual tax payable.

## 5. Do not

- Do not confirm whether a specific deduction succeeded or failed.
- Do not advise on bank charges — refer the taxpayer to their bank.
- Do not compute instalment amounts or outstanding balances.
- Do not state when a specific taxpayer's plan will be revised.

## 6. Related

- SOP-PAY-002
- SOP-ESC-002

# SOP-INC-001 - Rental income

> **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT.** Authored for a technical assessment. This is not an
> IRAS document and does not reflect IRAS internal material, templates or
> practice. Every factual claim is a restatement traceable to the public
> source cited beside it in section 2.

> **HELD OUT OF THE INDEX.** This procedure is authored but excluded from
> the runtime lookup, so the classes it serves resolve to no SOP. See
> `sop_design.md` S5.

## 1. Scope

Taxpayer asks whether rent received is taxable, when rental income must be declared, what expenses may be deducted, or how the simplified claim for rental expenses works.

**Not in scope:**
- The taxpayer's own declared rental figures or assessment. -> escalate (`account_specific`)
- Computing net rental income or tax for the taxpayer. -> escalate (`amount_computation_requested`)
- Property tax, which is a different tax type. -> escalate (`oos_other_agency`)

## 2. Key facts the officer may state

- Rent payments received from renting out a property are subject to income tax and must be declared in the Income Tax Return.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- Net rental income, after deduction of allowable expenses, is subject to income tax.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- Rental income is taxable from the date it is due and payable to the property owner, not the date it is actually received. Rent due in 2025 but paid in 2026 is declared for Year of Assessment 2026.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- Any amount recovered from insurance on a property that is rented out is taxable and should be reported as part of income.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- Under the simplified claim for rental expenses for tenanted residential property, deemed rental expenses calculated as 15% of gross rent are pre-filled in the online tax form.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- In addition to the 15% deemed rental expenses, property owners may still claim mortgage interest on the loan taken to purchase the property.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- The amount of taxable rental income depends on whether the property is solely or jointly owned.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>

## 3. Decision steps

1. **If** Asking about their own declared rental figures or assessment  
   -> Escalate (`account_specific`)
2. **If** Asking IRAS to compute net rental income or tax  
   -> Escalate (`amount_computation_requested`)
3. **If** Asking about property tax rather than income tax on rent  
   -> Redirect (`oos_other_agency`)
4. **If** Otherwise  
   -> State the treatment of rental income from the key facts

## 4. Approved phrasing

**`taxable`**

> Rent you receive from renting out your property is subject to income tax and must be declared in your Income Tax Return. It is the net rental income, after deducting allowable expenses, that is taxed.

**`timing`**

> Rental income is taxable from the date it is due and payable to you, rather than the date you actually receive it. For example, rent due to you in 2025 but paid in January 2026 is declared for Year of Assessment 2026.

**`simplified_expenses`**

> For tenanted residential property, a simplified claim is available: deemed rental expenses of 15% of your gross rent are pre-filled in the online tax form. You may still claim mortgage interest on the loan taken to purchase the property in addition to the 15%.

## 5. Do not

- Do not compute net rental income, allowable expenses or tax payable.
- Do not confirm a taxpayer's own declared figures.
- Do not advise whether the simplified claim or actual expenses is more advantageous for a particular taxpayer.
- Do not answer property tax questions from this procedure.

## 6. Related

- SOP-FIL-001
- SOP-RTE-002

# SOP-REL-005 - Personal income tax relief cap

> **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT.** Authored for a technical assessment. This is not an
> IRAS document and does not reflect IRAS internal material, templates or
> practice. Every factual claim is a restatement traceable to the public
> source cited beside it in section 2.

> **HELD OUT OF THE INDEX.** This procedure is authored but excluded from
> the runtime lookup, so the classes it serves resolve to no SOP. See
> `sop_design.md` S5.

## 1. Scope

Taxpayer asks whether there is a limit on the total amount of personal reliefs they may claim, how the cap applies across different reliefs, or what happens when their claims exceed it.

**Not in scope:**
- Whether this taxpayer's own reliefs exceed the cap, and by how much. -> escalate (`account_specific`)
- Computing the taxpayer's total reliefs or resulting tax. -> escalate (`amount_computation_requested`)

## 2. Key facts the officer may state

- A personal income tax relief cap of $80,000 applies to the total amount of all tax reliefs claimed for each Year of Assessment.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- A taxpayer is affected by the cap if the total amount of personal reliefs they claim exceeds $80,000.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- The overall personal income tax relief cap takes effect from Year of Assessment 2018.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- The cap applies to the total of all personal reliefs taken together. It is not a limit within any single relief, so it cannot be determined from the rules of one relief alone.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- Where the cap applies, the reliefs allowed are limited to $80,000, and this is reflected in the Notice of Assessment.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- The cap applies to the total of all reliefs, including relief on compulsory and voluntary CPF contributions.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- The $80,000 cap operates on top of the individual caps within specific reliefs, such as the $50,000 per-child cap on QCR or Child Relief (Disability) combined with WMCR.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/working-mother's-child-relief-(wmcr)</sup>
- There is no refund of accepted voluntary CPF or SRS contributions where the relief cap means they attract no tax relief.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>

## 3. Decision steps

1. **If** Asking whether their own reliefs exceed the cap  
   -> Escalate (`account_specific`)
2. **If** Asking IRAS to total their reliefs or compute the effect of the cap  
   -> Escalate (`amount_computation_requested`)
3. **If** Otherwise  
   -> State the cap and how it applies from the key facts

## 4. Approved phrasing

**`cap`**

> A personal income tax relief cap of $80,000 applies to the total amount of all tax reliefs you claim in each Year of Assessment. If the total of your personal reliefs exceeds $80,000, the reliefs allowed to you are limited to $80,000, and this is reflected in your Notice of Assessment.

**`interaction`**

> The $80,000 cap applies on top of the caps within individual reliefs, such as the $50,000 combined cap per child on Qualifying Child Relief and Working Mother's Child Relief.

**`no_refund`**

> Please note that voluntary CPF and SRS contributions cannot be refunded if the relief cap means they do not attract tax relief, so it is worth considering the cap before making a voluntary contribution.

## 5. Do not

- Do not total a taxpayer's reliefs or compute the effect of the cap for them.
- Do not confirm whether a specific taxpayer is affected by the cap.
- Do not advise whether a voluntary contribution is financially worthwhile.

## 6. Related

- SOP-REL-001
- SOP-REL-002
- SOP-REL-003
- SOP-REL-004

# Data sources, licensing, and privacy

Every input to this project, where it came from, what licence governs it, and what
was done to it. Nothing in `data/` is real citizen correspondence.

---

## 1. Summary

| Asset | Origin | Committed? | Licence position |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data/sop/*.md` — 17 SOPs | **Authored by me**, facts traced to public IRAS pages | Yes | Original work. Facts are not copyrightable. |
| `data/scenarios/*.yaml` — 116 situations | **Authored by me** | Yes | Original work. |
| `data/generated/emails.jsonl` — 3,000 emails | Generated by GPT-4o from the scenario specs | Yes | Model output; OpenAI grants output rights to the caller. |
| `data/splits/splits.json` | Derived, seeded | Yes | Derived artefact. |
| IRAS guidance pages (30 URLs) | `iras.gov.sg` | **No — gitignored** | Read as reference only. Not redistributed. |
| CFPB Consumer Complaint Database | Accessed through Hugging Face | **No** | Read for register/style only; no complaint text is retained, redistributed, or used for training/evaluation. |
| `models/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` | Hugging Face | Yes | Apache 2.0; upstream licence and attribution are included beside the weights. |

---

## 2. The SOP corpus — authored, not scraped

**No agency publishes its internal SOPs.** Any honest version of this project must
author them, and pretending otherwise would be the more serious misrepresentation.

Each of the 17 SOPs is a **synthetic officer-facing procedure**. Every factual claim
in one traces to a public IRAS URL recorded in that file's `references:` frontmatter —
**30 distinct URLs**, all on `www.iras.gov.sg`.

Three structural guarantees, enforced at load time rather than by convention:

- **Every SOP carries a synthetic banner.** `src/triage/sop/loader.py` raises at
  startup if `synthetic: true` is missing. A corpus that could be mistaken for real
  agency material is the failure mode this guards against.
- **Every SOP must declare at least one reference.** An empty `references:` list is a
  hard load error.
- **Citations are checked, not assumed.** `python scripts/generate_sops.py --check`
  validates that all 148 recorded facts resolve to a declared source. It is a
  Makefile target and part of the normal build.

None of these files reflects internal IRAS material, template, or practice. They are
my reconstruction of what such a procedure would plausibly contain. The
[SOP authoring schema](sop_specs/README.md) is the integration point through which a
real agency could provide its own procedures without changing application code.

### 2.1 How the reference pages were used

`scripts/fetch_reference.py` fetches the registry of public pages into `.scratch/`,
which is **gitignored** (`.gitignore` line 3). The manifest records the URL, fetch date
(2026-09-01), HTTP status and byte count for each.

The fetched HTML exists **only** so that facts written into the SOP specs can be
checked against their source during human review. It is never committed, never
redistributed, and never fed to a model.

Politeness measures: a courtesy rate-limit between requests (`--delay`, default
applied in the fetch loop), a single pass rather than a crawl, and a fixed registry of
~30 named pages rather than link-following. A browser User-Agent is set because the
IRAS site serves a JavaScript navigation shell to unknown agents and returns no
content otherwise — this is to receive the page a human would see, not to evade a
restriction.

`https://www.iras.gov.sg/robots.txt` was checked on **2026-09-03** and returned HTTP
404, so there were no published crawler directives to apply. Absence of a robots file
is not treated as permission: the fixed allowlist, one-second delay, single pass, and
Terms-of-Use analysis below still govern the fetch.

### 2.2 Licensing position, stated plainly

IRAS Terms of Use restrict reproduction of site contents. Read literally, they also
require written permission to hyperlink to an internal page — a provision that reads
as boilerplate and is not observed in practice anywhere on the Singapore web.

**This project does not depend on resolving that question**, because it does not
reproduce site content. The operative principle is that **copyright protects
expression, not facts**. A filing deadline, a relief cap, and a penalty rate are facts
stated in or derived from legislation; they are not anyone's creative expression.

What is committed is my own prose restating those facts, with a citation to where each
came from. What is not committed is any IRAS page, in whole or in part.

**Note on figures.** Relief caps and rates in the SOPs are stated as the public pages
state them. They are a snapshot taken 2026-09-01 and will go stale — a production
version would need effective-date metadata and a re-indexing cadence, which is listed
under future improvements in the README.

---

## 3. Synthetic emails

3,000 emails generated by **GPT-4o** from 116 hand-authored scenario specifications.

### 3.1 Why synthetic

Real citizen correspondence to a tax authority contains NRICs, addresses, income
figures and financial distress. It cannot be obtained lawfully for a take-home
exercise, cannot be ethically used if it could, and no public corpus of Singapore
government email enquiries exists. Synthetic is the only honest option here, and the
question becomes whether it is generated well enough to support a claim.

### 3.2 What makes it defensible

**The generator never sees the label.** It receives a *situation* description
("someone received a message claiming to be from the tax authority asking them to
confirm bank details, and wants to know if it is real"). The class label is attached
afterward from the scenario file. The model cannot write toward a class name, which is
the mechanism that would otherwise plant a giveaway token in every email of a class.

**Three independent axes of variation:**

- *Content* — persona, life situation, and the guidance actually relevant to it.
- *Style* — standard English; imperfect English with typos, run-ons and all-caps;
  lightly Singlish-inflected. Register calibrated against sampled real CFPB complaints
  (read for tone; no text copied).
- *Season* — filing period, estimates, notice-of-assessment period.

Plus an edge-case slice: answerable only from held-out guidance, account-specific
phrasing, and genuine edge cases recalled from prior call-centre experience.

**Model separation.** The generator (OpenAI GPT-4o) differs from the zero-shot
classification baseline and the groundedness judge (both Groq/Qwen). No model in the
evaluation path is ever scored on text it wrote — enforced as an explicit rule in
`config/models.yaml`.

### 3.3 Leakage is tested, not assumed

`python scripts/check_leakage.py` runs seven checks over the committed corpus. All
seven pass on the current one:

0. **Balance** — class counts against the taxonomy (300 per class × 10).
1. **Vocabulary leakage** — a TF-IDF + logistic-regression probe. It should classify
   *well but not perfectly*: a near-perfect score means a giveaway token exists and the
   corpus needs regenerating. Measured accuracy sits in the expected band.
2. **System vocabulary** — no email contains the system's own terms (bucket names,
   SOP ids, class names).
3. **Length as a giveaway** — that message length alone does not carry class signal.
4. **Near-duplicates** — cosine similarity across the corpus.
5. **Boilerplate** — that generated openings and closings do not cluster by class.
6. **Flag confounding** — that a lexical flag is not standing in for a class.

Separately, **splits are grouped by `scenario_id`**, so every variant of a situation
lands in the same split and no paraphrase straddles the train/test boundary. That is
enforced in `scripts/make_splits.py` and verified by zero scenario overlap between
every pair of splits.

### 3.4 Privacy in the generated data

- **All identifiers were generated for the project, not sourced from people.** NRICs
  are checksum-valid so the detector can be tested honestly. The values were not
  checked against official registries, so accidental collision cannot be ruled out.
- Addresses combine public Singapore street and estate names with generated block and
  unit numbers. Phone numbers and postal codes are generated in valid-looking shapes.
- No personal identifier belonging to the author or a known person was used.
- **What was planted is recorded** (`plant_pii` per email), which is what makes scrub
  recall measurable rather than asserted.

### 3.5 Privacy in the pipeline itself

Beyond the data, three properties of the system:

- **Scrubbing happens before any external call.** The classifier and the drafter both
  see placeholder text; real values never leave the machine. Rehydration is local and
  happens after the network call, in exactly one place.
- **No PII in committed results.** `eval/metrics/pii_recall.py` masks missed values at
  the point of capture (`S0433218J` → `S0*****8J`), so the module that measures
  containment cannot itself write an identifier into `eval/results/`.
- **`.env` is gitignored** and `triage.env.key_status()` reports only booleans, never
  key values.

---

## 4. CFPB Consumer Complaint Database

- **Source:** [US Consumer Financial Protection Bureau complaint
  database](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/data-research/consumer-complaints/),
  accessed through a Hugging Face copy during style review.
- **Privacy:** CFPB publishes complaint narratives only after removing personal
  information. No narrative is stored or redistributed by this project.
- **Use:** read to calibrate *register* — how members of the public actually write to
  an institution when frustrated, confused, or in financial difficulty. Sentence
  length, politeness markers, how a complaint opens.
- **Not used for:** training, evaluation, or text reuse. No CFPB text appears in this
  repository. It is American and about consumer finance, so it is a style reference
  only, never a content one.

---

## 5. Model weights

- **`sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`** — Apache 2.0, from Hugging Face.
  Committed to the repo (~88 MB fine-tuned) so a clone yields real weights rather than
  git-lfs pointers. The upstream licence and attribution notice are included beside
  both the base encoder and the fine-tuned derivative.
- Gemini, Groq and OpenAI are accessed by API under their respective terms. No weights
  are redistributed.

---

## 6. What this data does not cover

Recorded here as well as in the README, because it bounds every number reported:

- **116 situations is the binding constraint**, not 3,000 emails. Per-class figures
  rest on ~90 test emails drawn from a handful of situations each, so a class can look
  strong because its few situations happen to be easy.
- **A synthetic ceiling.** This measures performance on a distribution GPT-4o and I
  jointly imagined. It cannot tell you a real inbox looks like this — that is the one
  thing this project cannot check about itself.
- **One agency, one tax type.** Individual income tax only. No corporate tax, GST,
  property tax, or stamp duty.
- **English only**, with Singlish inflection. No Chinese, Malay or Tamil.
- **No attachments, no threads, no forwarded chains.** Every email is a single
  standalone message, which real correspondence often is not.
- **Author-shaped distribution.** The scenario set reflects what I judged
  representative. A real inbox would be shaped by seasonality, campaigns, and
  events nobody anticipated.

The most valuable next data step is not more emails — it is **more situations**, and a
validation-only slice of real anonymised enquiries to test whether the synthetic
situation set resembles the real one.

# SOP-PAY-001 - Handling GIRO enquiries

> **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT.** Authored for a technical assessment. This is not an
> IRAS document and does not reflect IRAS internal material, templates or
> practice. Every factual claim is a restatement traceable to the public
> source cited beside it in section 2.

## 1. Scope

Taxpayer asks how GIRO works, how to apply, when deductions occur, what happens when a deduction fails, how the provisional instalment plan works, or how to edit, cancel or re-activate an arrangement.

**Not in scope:**
- The status of a specific taxpayer's GIRO plan, or why their deduction failed. -> escalate (`account_specific`)
- Restructuring instalments because the taxpayer cannot afford them. -> escalate (`hardship_or_waiver_request`)
- Computing an instalment amount for a specific taxpayer. -> escalate (`amount_computation_requested`)

## 2. Key facts the officer may state

- Tax may be paid by GIRO either in monthly instalments of up to 12 months, or as a one-time yearly payment.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- Monthly GIRO deductions are made on the 6th of each month.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- If the deduction date falls on a weekend or public holiday, the deduction is made on the next working day.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- If a GIRO deduction is unsuccessful, a second deduction is attempted on the 20th of the month.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- A GIRO arrangement is cancelled after 2 consecutive months of failed deductions, that is, 4 failed deductions in a row.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- The Provisional Instalment Plan (PIP) commences yearly from May, based on the previous year's tax or the current year's estimated tax payable.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- Once the assessment is finalised, the monthly GIRO arrangement is revised based on the actual tax payable.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- Where a taxpayer joins GIRO after May, instalment deductions commence in the month after the application is approved and end in April of the following year.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- eGIRO applications may be made through myTax Portal (set up within minutes), through the DBS/POSB, OCBC or UOB bank portals (within 3 working days), or at AXS stations (within 3 working days).  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- Hard copy GIRO applications require up to 21 working days to process, and the exact timeline is subject to the respective bank's processing.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- GIRO must be applied for using an SGD savings or current account with a participating bank.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- For a successful deduction the account must hold sufficient funds on the deduction date and have a suitable payment limit set. Some banks may impose charges for unsuccessful GIRO deductions.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- A cancelled GIRO arrangement may be re-activated through the 'Apply/Manage GIRO Plan' digital service at myTax Portal.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>
- To terminate a GIRO arrangement entirely, the taxpayer must contact their bank directly; a cancelled arrangement can still be re-activated with IRAS.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax</sup>

## 3. Decision steps

1. **If** Asking about their own plan, a specific failed deduction, or their own instalment amount  
   -> Escalate (`account_specific`)
2. **If** Requesting penalty waiver, or restructuring because they cannot afford the instalments  
   -> Escalate (`hardship_or_waiver_request`)
3. **If** Asking IRAS to calculate an instalment amount or a balance  
   -> Escalate (`amount_computation_requested`)
4. **If** Otherwise  
   -> Answer from the key facts and direct to the application channels

## 4. Approved phrasing

**`giro_dates`**

> Payments by GIRO are deducted on the 6th of each month. If the 6th falls on a weekend or public holiday, the deduction is made on the next working day. Where a deduction is unsuccessful, a second attempt is made on the 20th of the month.

**`giro_failure`**

> A GIRO arrangement is cancelled after two consecutive months of failed deductions, that is, four failed deductions in a row. Please ensure that your account holds sufficient funds on the deduction date and that a suitable payment limit is set. If your arrangement has been cancelled, you may re-activate it through the 'Apply/Manage GIRO Plan' digital service at myTax Portal.

**`giro_apply`**

> You can apply for eGIRO through myTax Portal, which is set up within minutes, or through the DBS/POSB, OCBC and UOB bank portals and AXS stations, which take up to 3 working days. GIRO must be set up using an SGD savings or current account with a participating bank.

**`pip`**

> The Provisional Instalment Plan begins in May each year and is based on the previous year's tax or the current year's estimated tax payable. Once your assessment is finalised, your monthly instalments are revised to reflect the actual tax payable.

## 5. Do not

- Do not confirm whether a specific deduction succeeded or failed.
- Do not advise on bank charges — refer the taxpayer to their bank.
- Do not compute instalment amounts or outstanding balances.
- Do not state when a specific taxpayer's plan will be revised.

## 6. Related

- SOP-PAY-002
- SOP-ESC-002

# SOP-INC-001 - Rental income

> **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT.** Authored for a technical assessment. This is not an
> IRAS document and does not reflect IRAS internal material, templates or
> practice. Every factual claim is a restatement traceable to the public
> source cited beside it in section 2.

> **HELD OUT OF THE INDEX.** This procedure is authored but excluded from
> the runtime lookup, so the classes it serves resolve to no SOP. See
> `sop_design.md` S5.

## 1. Scope

Taxpayer asks whether rent received is taxable, when rental income must be declared, what expenses may be deducted, or how the simplified claim for rental expenses works.

**Not in scope:**
- The taxpayer's own declared rental figures or assessment. -> escalate (`account_specific`)
- Computing net rental income or tax for the taxpayer. -> escalate (`amount_computation_requested`)
- Property tax, which is a different tax type. -> escalate (`oos_other_agency`)

## 2. Key facts the officer may state

- Rent payments received from renting out a property are subject to income tax and must be declared in the Income Tax Return.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- Net rental income, after deduction of allowable expenses, is subject to income tax.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- Rental income is taxable from the date it is due and payable to the property owner, not the date it is actually received. Rent due in 2025 but paid in 2026 is declared for Year of Assessment 2026.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- Any amount recovered from insurance on a property that is rented out is taxable and should be reported as part of income.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- Under the simplified claim for rental expenses for tenanted residential property, deemed rental expenses calculated as 15% of gross rent are pre-filled in the online tax form.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- In addition to the 15% deemed rental expenses, property owners may still claim mortgage interest on the loan taken to purchase the property.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>
- The amount of taxable rental income depends on whether the property is solely or jointly owned.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/income-from-property-rented-out</sup>

## 3. Decision steps

1. **If** Asking about their own declared rental figures or assessment  
   -> Escalate (`account_specific`)
2. **If** Asking IRAS to compute net rental income or tax  
   -> Escalate (`amount_computation_requested`)
3. **If** Asking about property tax rather than income tax on rent  
   -> Redirect (`oos_other_agency`)
4. **If** Otherwise  
   -> State the treatment of rental income from the key facts

## 4. Approved phrasing

**`taxable`**

> Rent you receive from renting out your property is subject to income tax and must be declared in your Income Tax Return. It is the net rental income, after deducting allowable expenses, that is taxed.

**`timing`**

> Rental income is taxable from the date it is due and payable to you, rather than the date you actually receive it. For example, rent due to you in 2025 but paid in January 2026 is declared for Year of Assessment 2026.

**`simplified_expenses`**

> For tenanted residential property, a simplified claim is available: deemed rental expenses of 15% of your gross rent are pre-filled in the online tax form. You may still claim mortgage interest on the loan taken to purchase the property in addition to the 15%.

## 5. Do not

- Do not compute net rental income, allowable expenses or tax payable.
- Do not confirm a taxpayer's own declared figures.
- Do not advise whether the simplified claim or actual expenses is more advantageous for a particular taxpayer.
- Do not answer property tax questions from this procedure.

## 6. Related

- SOP-FIL-001
- SOP-RTE-002

# SOP-REL-005 - Personal income tax relief cap

> **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT.** Authored for a technical assessment. This is not an
> IRAS document and does not reflect IRAS internal material, templates or
> practice. Every factual claim is a restatement traceable to the public
> source cited beside it in section 2.

> **HELD OUT OF THE INDEX.** This procedure is authored but excluded from
> the runtime lookup, so the classes it serves resolve to no SOP. See
> `sop_design.md` S5.

## 1. Scope

Taxpayer asks whether there is a limit on the total amount of personal reliefs they may claim, how the cap applies across different reliefs, or what happens when their claims exceed it.

**Not in scope:**
- Whether this taxpayer's own reliefs exceed the cap, and by how much. -> escalate (`account_specific`)
- Computing the taxpayer's total reliefs or resulting tax. -> escalate (`amount_computation_requested`)

## 2. Key facts the officer may state

- A personal income tax relief cap of $80,000 applies to the total amount of all tax reliefs claimed for each Year of Assessment.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- A taxpayer is affected by the cap if the total amount of personal reliefs they claim exceeds $80,000.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- The overall personal income tax relief cap takes effect from Year of Assessment 2018.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- The cap applies to the total of all personal reliefs taken together. It is not a limit within any single relief, so it cannot be determined from the rules of one relief alone.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- Where the cap applies, the reliefs allowed are limited to $80,000, and this is reflected in the Notice of Assessment.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- The cap applies to the total of all reliefs, including relief on compulsory and voluntary CPF contributions.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>
- The $80,000 cap operates on top of the individual caps within specific reliefs, such as the $50,000 per-child cap on QCR or Child Relief (Disability) combined with WMCR.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/working-mother's-child-relief-(wmcr)</sup>
- There is no refund of accepted voluntary CPF or SRS contributions where the relief cap means they attract no tax relief.  
  <sup>Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs</sup>

## 3. Decision steps

1. **If** Asking whether their own reliefs exceed the cap  
   -> Escalate (`account_specific`)
2. **If** Asking IRAS to total their reliefs or compute the effect of the cap  
   -> Escalate (`amount_computation_requested`)
3. **If** Otherwise  
   -> State the cap and how it applies from the key facts

## 4. Approved phrasing

**`cap`**

> A personal income tax relief cap of $80,000 applies to the total amount of all tax reliefs you claim in each Year of Assessment. If the total of your personal reliefs exceeds $80,000, the reliefs allowed to you are limited to $80,000, and this is reflected in your Notice of Assessment.

**`interaction`**

> The $80,000 cap applies on top of the caps within individual reliefs, such as the $50,000 combined cap per child on Qualifying Child Relief and Working Mother's Child Relief.

**`no_refund`**

> Please note that voluntary CPF and SRS contributions cannot be refunded if the relief cap means they do not attract tax relief, so it is worth considering the cap before making a voluntary contribution.

## 5. Do not

- Do not total a taxpayer's reliefs or compute the effect of the cap for them.
- Do not confirm whether a specific taxpayer is affected by the cap.
- Do not advise whether a voluntary contribution is financially worthwhile.

## 6. Related

- SOP-REL-001
- SOP-REL-002
- SOP-REL-003
- SOP-REL-004

1	"""Render ``data/sop_specs/*.yaml`` into the SOP corpus at ``data/sop/*.md``.
2	
3	BUILD-TIME ONLY. Never imported by ``src/``.
4	
5	The specs are the source of truth; the markdown is derived and must never be
6	hand-edited. Running this script is idempotent, so a spec change plus a re-run is
7	the only way the corpus changes.
8	
9	Why generate rather than author markdown directly: the public-URL traceability
10	guarantee (``sop_design.md`` S8.2) is enforced here, not promised in a README.
11	Every fact carries a ``source`` handle, this script refuses to render a fact whose
12	handle does not resolve to a cited reference, and the rendered S2 prints the URL
13	beside the claim. A reviewer can therefore check any sentence in the corpus
14	against a page without leaving the file.
15	
16	Three build-time checks run before anything is written, each guarding a design
17	property that would fail silently if it broke:
18	
19	1. **Citations resolve.**  No fact may cite a handle absent from ``references``.
20	2. **The relief-cap holdout does not leak.**  No *indexed* spec may state the
21	   $80,000 personal relief cap as a fact. The cap is a property of the sum of all
22	   reliefs, so it cannot be derived from any single relief's rules — which is
23	   what makes SOP-REL-005 a genuine partial-answer holdout. If an indexed SOP
24	   restated it, the agent could answer the cap question from the index and the
25	   holdout would collapse into an ordinary answerable case.
26	3. **Held-out classes stay empty.**  ``rental_income`` and ``foreign_income_dta``
27	   must resolve to no indexed SOP, so that ``no_supporting_sop`` is *derived*
28	   from an empty lookup rather than hand-mapped (``BUILD.md`` S5.6).
29	
30	Usage:
31	    python scripts/generate_sops.py            # render the corpus
32	    python scripts/generate_sops.py --check    # validate only, write nothing
33	"""
34	
35	from __future__ import annotations
36	
37	import argparse
38	import re
39	import sys
40	from pathlib import Path
41	from typing import Any, Final
42	
43	import yaml
44	
45	ROOT: Final[Path] = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
46	SPEC_DIR: Final[Path] = ROOT / "data" / "sop_specs"
47	OUT_DIR: Final[Path] = ROOT / "data" / "sop"
48	
49	#: Classes deliberately excluded from the index, yielding `no_supporting_sop`.
50	#: Listed here so the generator fails loudly if a holdout is ever un-held by
51	#: accident — the holdout is a design commitment, not an oversight.
52	HELD_OUT_CLASSES: Final[frozenset[str]] = frozenset({"rental_income", "foreign_income_dta"})
53	
54	#: Marker for the leakage guard described in the module docstring.
55	RELIEF_CAP_MARKER: Final[str] = "80,000"
56	
57	#: Prepended to every rendered SOP. The misrepresentation guard: a synthetic SOP
58	#: that reads like a real IRAS document is its own problem (`sop_design.md` S8.2).
59	BANNER: Final[str] = (
60	    "> **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT.** Authored for a technical assessment. This is not an\n"
61	    "> IRAS document and does not reflect IRAS internal material, templates or\n"
62	    "> practice. Every factual claim is a restatement traceable to the public\n"
63	    "> source cited beside it in section 2.\n"
64	)
65	
66	
67	class SpecError(RuntimeError):
68	    """A spec violates a build-time guarantee."""
69	
70	
71	def load_specs() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
72	    """Load every spec, sorted by ``sop_id`` for deterministic output."""
73	    specs = [
74	        yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
75	        for path in sorted(SPEC_DIR.glob("*.yaml"))
76	    ]
77	    return sorted(specs, key=lambda spec: spec["sop_id"])
78	
79	
80	def check_citations(spec: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
81	    """Return an error for every fact citing an unknown reference handle."""
82	    handles = {ref["id"] for ref in spec.get("references", [])}
83	    return [
84	        f"{spec['sop_id']}: fact cites unknown source {fact.get('source')!r} "
85	        f"-- {fact['text'][:60].strip()}..."
86	        for fact in spec.get("facts", [])
87	        if fact.get("source") not in handles
88	    ]
89	
90	
91	def check_relief_cap_leak(spec: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
92	    """Return an error if an indexed spec states the global relief cap as a fact."""
93	    if not spec["indexed"]:
94	        return []
95	    return [
96	        f"{spec['sop_id']}: indexed spec states the ${RELIEF_CAP_MARKER} relief cap, "
97	        f"which belongs to the held-out SOP-REL-005 -- {fact['text'][:60].strip()}..."
98	        for fact in spec.get("facts", [])
99	        if RELIEF_CAP_MARKER in fact["text"]
100	    ]
101	
102	
103	def build_index(specs: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
104	    """Map each class to its INDEXED SOPs. Held-out SOPs are excluded by design."""
105	    index: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
106	    for spec in specs:
107	        if not spec["indexed"]:
108	            continue
109	        for intent in spec["intents"]:
110	            index.setdefault(intent, []).append(spec["sop_id"])
111	    return index
112	
113	
114	def check_holdouts(index: dict[str, list[str]]) -> list[str]:
115	    """Return an error if a held-out class resolved to any indexed SOP."""
116	    return [
117	        f"{cls}: expected no indexed SOP (holdout), found {index[cls]}"
118	        for cls in sorted(HELD_OUT_CLASSES)
119	        if cls in index
120	    ]
121	
122	
123	def validate(specs: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[str]:
124	    """Run every build-time check and return all errors found."""
125	    errors: list[str] = []
126	    for spec in specs:
127	        errors += check_citations(spec)
128	        errors += check_relief_cap_leak(spec)
129	    errors += check_holdouts(build_index(specs))
130	    return errors
S1:1	# SOP-RTE-001 — Redirect: business and corporate income tax
S1:2	#
S1:3	# Class: oos_business_tax. Bucket: out_of_scope.
S1:4	#
S1:5	# "NO BACK DOOR" (sop_design.md S2.3). The redirect is the correct outcome, not a
S1:6	# failure — and because it is an automated action, it COUNTS TOWARD COVERAGE
S1:7	# (BUILD.md S5.6). The system is scoped to individual income tax; answering a
S1:8	# corporate question from IIT knowledge would be the failure.
S1:9	#
S1:10	# `auto_reply_permitted: true` — unlike ESC-*, this class DOES auto-reply, with a
S1:11	# redirect. Its bucket has a threshold that bites, so a low-confidence redirect
S1:12	# still escalates rather than sending the citizen to the wrong place.
S1:13	#
S1:14	# KEPT SEPARATE FROM RTE-002 by review decision: the granularity principle would
S1:15	# merge them (identical routing), but the redirect destinations are unrelated —
S1:16	# another IRAS tax type versus another agency entirely — and a wrong redirect is a
S1:17	# visible citizen-facing failure. Cost accepted: one confusable pair, ~4 fewer
S1:18	# test examples per class.
S1:19	
S1:20	sop_id: SOP-RTE-001
S1:21	title: "Redirect: business and corporate income tax"
S1:22	version: "1.0"
S1:23	effective_date: 2026-01-01
S1:24	supersedes: null
S1:25	applies_to_ya: [2025, 2026]
S1:26	intents: [oos_business_tax]
S1:27	indexed: true
S1:28	owner_queue: IIT-General          # INVENTED — not a real IRAS queue
S1:29	handling_target: same_day         # ILLUSTRATIVE — not a real IRAS SLA
S1:30	auto_reply_permitted: true
S1:31	escalate_if:
S1:32	  - account_specific
S1:33	  - amount_computation_requested
S1:34	
S1:35	references:

1	"""Render ``data/sop_specs/*.yaml`` into the SOP corpus at ``data/sop/*.md``.
2	
3	BUILD-TIME ONLY. Never imported by ``src/``.
4	
5	The specs are the source of truth; the markdown is derived and must never be
6	hand-edited. Running this script is idempotent, so a spec change plus a re-run is
7	the only way the corpus changes.
8	
9	Why generate rather than author markdown directly: the public-URL traceability
10	guarantee (``sop_design.md`` S8.2) is enforced here, not promised in a README.
11	Every fact carries a ``source`` handle, this script refuses to render a fact whose
12	handle does not resolve to a cited reference, and the rendered S2 prints the URL
13	beside the claim. A reviewer can therefore check any sentence in the corpus
14	against a page without leaving the file.
15	
16	Three build-time checks run before anything is written, each guarding a design
17	property that would fail silently if it broke:
18	
19	1. **Citations resolve.**  No fact may cite a handle absent from ``references``.
20	2. **The relief-cap holdout does not leak.**  No *indexed* spec may state the
21	   $80,000 personal relief cap as a fact. The cap is a property of the sum of all
22	   reliefs, so it cannot be derived from any single relief's rules — which is
23	   what makes SOP-REL-005 a genuine partial-answer holdout. If an indexed SOP
24	   restated it, the agent could answer the cap question from the index and the
25	   holdout would collapse into an ordinary answerable case.
26	3. **Held-out classes stay empty.**  ``rental_income`` and ``foreign_income_dta``
27	   must resolve to no indexed SOP, so that ``no_supporting_sop`` is *derived*
28	   from an empty lookup rather than hand-mapped (``BUILD.md`` S5.6).
29	
30	Usage:
31	    python scripts/generate_sops.py            # render the corpus
32	    python scripts/generate_sops.py --check    # validate only, write nothing
33	"""
34	
35	from __future__ import annotations
36	
37	import argparse
38	import re
39	import sys
40	from pathlib import Path
41	from typing import Any, Final
42	
43	import yaml
44	
45	ROOT: Final[Path] = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
46	SPEC_DIR: Final[Path] = ROOT / "data" / "sop_specs"
47	OUT_DIR: Final[Path] = ROOT / "data" / "sop"
48	
49	#: Classes deliberately excluded from the index, yielding `no_supporting_sop`.
50	#: Listed here so the generator fails loudly if a holdout is ever un-held by
51	#: accident — the holdout is a design commitment, not an oversight.
52	HELD_OUT_CLASSES: Final[frozenset[str]] = frozenset({"rental_income", "foreign_income_dta"})
53	
54	#: Marker for the leakage guard described in the module docstring.
55	RELIEF_CAP_MARKER: Final[str] = "80,000"
56	
57	#: Prepended to every rendered SOP. The misrepresentation guard: a synthetic SOP
58	#: that reads like a real IRAS document is its own problem (`sop_design.md` S8.2).
59	BANNER: Final[str] = (
60	    "> **SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT.** Authored for a technical assessment. This is not an\n"
61	    "> IRAS document and does not reflect IRAS internal material, templates or\n"
62	    "> practice. Every factual claim is a restatement traceable to the public\n"
63	    "> source cited beside it in section 2.\n"
64	)
65	
66	
67	class SpecError(RuntimeError):
68	    """A spec violates a build-time guarantee."""
69	
70	
71	def load_specs() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
72	    """Load every spec, sorted by ``sop_id`` for deterministic output."""
73	    specs = [
74	        yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
75	        for path in sorted(SPEC_DIR.glob("*.yaml"))
76	    ]
77	    return sorted(specs, key=lambda spec: spec["sop_id"])
78	
79	
80	def check_citations(spec: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
81	    """Return an error for every fact citing an unknown reference handle."""
82	    handles = {ref["id"] for ref in spec.get("references", [])}
83	    return [
84	        f"{spec['sop_id']}: fact cites unknown source {fact.get('source')!r} "
85	        f"-- {fact['text'][:60].strip()}..."
86	        for fact in spec.get("facts", [])
87	        if fact.get("source") not in handles
88	    ]
89	
90	
91	def check_relief_cap_leak(spec: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
92	    """Return an error if an indexed spec states the global relief cap as a fact."""
93	    if not spec["indexed"]:
94	        return []
95	    return [
96	        f"{spec['sop_id']}: indexed spec states the ${RELIEF_CAP_MARKER} relief cap, "
97	        f"which belongs to the held-out SOP-REL-005 -- {fact['text'][:60].strip()}..."
98	        for fact in spec.get("facts", [])
99	        if RELIEF_CAP_MARKER in fact["text"]
100	    ]
101	
102	
103	def build_index(specs: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
104	    """Map each class to its INDEXED SOPs. Held-out SOPs are excluded by design."""
105	    index: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
106	    for spec in specs:
107	        if not spec["indexed"]:
108	            continue
109	        for intent in spec["intents"]:
110	            index.setdefault(intent, []).append(spec["sop_id"])
111	    return index
112	
113	
114	def check_holdouts(index: dict[str, list[str]]) -> list[str]:
115	    """Return an error if a held-out class resolved to any indexed SOP."""
116	    return [
117	        f"{cls}: expected no indexed SOP (holdout), found {index[cls]}"
118	        for cls in sorted(HELD_OUT_CLASSES)
119	        if cls in index
120	    ]
121	
122	
123	def validate(specs: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[str]:
124	    """Run every build-time check and return all errors found."""
125	    errors: list[str] = []
126	    for spec in specs:
127	        errors += check_citations(spec)
128	        errors += check_relief_cap_leak(spec)
129	    errors += check_holdouts(build_index(specs))
130	    return errors

80	def check_citations(spec: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
81	    """Return an error for every fact citing an unknown reference handle."""
82	    handles = {ref["id"] for ref in spec.get("references", [])}
83	    return [

86	        for fact in spec.get("facts", [])
87	        if fact.get("source") not in handles
88	    ]

91	def check_relief_cap_leak(spec: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
92	    """Return an error if an indexed spec states the global relief cap as a fact."""
93	    if not spec["indexed"]:
94	        return []
95	    return [
96	        f"{spec['sop_id']}: indexed spec states the ${RELIEF_CAP_MARKER} relief cap, "
97	        f"which belongs to the held-out SOP-REL-005 -- {fact['text'][:60].strip()}..."
98	        for fact in spec.get("facts", [])
99	        if RELIEF_CAP_MARKER in fact["text"]
100	    ]

104	    """Map each class to its INDEXED SOPs. Held-out SOPs are excluded by design."""
105	    index: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
106	    for spec in specs:

115	    """Return an error if a held-out class resolved to any indexed SOP."""

+# Data sources, licensing, and privacy
+
+Nothing in \`data/\` is real citizen correspondence or an internal agency procedure.
+
+## Inventory
+
+| Asset | Origin | Use and licence position |
+|---|---|---|
+| \`data/sop/*.md\` | 17 author-written synthetic SOPs | Original wording based on public IRAS facts; source pages are cited, not copied |
+| \`data/scenarios/*.yaml\` | 116 author-written situations | Inputs for synthetic email generation |
+| \`data/generated/emails.jsonl\` | 3,000 GPT-4o outputs | Training and evaluation corpus |
+| \`data/splits/splits.json\` | Seeded, scenario-grouped split | 1,477 train / 646 calibration / 877 test |
+| IRAS guidance | 30 public URLs | Fact-checking only; fetched pages are not committed or redistributed |
+| CFPB complaints | Public database, accessed through Hugging Face | Writing-style reference only; no complaint text is retained or reused |
+| MiniLM-L6 | Hugging Face | Apache 2.0; see the [base-model notice](../models/all-MiniLM-L6-v2/NOTICE.md) and [fine-tuned-model notice](../models/classifier/NOTICE.md) |
+
+## Synthetic SOPs
+
+- The SOPs are not scraped and do not represent IRAS internal material, wording, queues, or service levels.
+- Each of 148 facts names a public IRAS source in its YAML spec.
+- \`python scripts/generate_sops.py --check\` rejects missing source handles and broken holdout rules.
