# Data sources, licensing, and privacy

Every input to this project, where it came from, what licence governs it, and what
was done to it. Nothing in `data/` is real citizen correspondence.

---

## 1. Summary

| Asset | Origin | Committed? | Licence position |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data/sop/*.md` — 17 SOPs | **Authored by me**, facts traced to public IRAS pages | Yes | Original work. Facts are not copyrightable. |
| `data/scenarios/*.yaml` — 116 situations | **Authored by me** | Yes | Original work. |
| `data/generated/emails.jsonl` — 3,000 emails | Generated by GPT-4o from the scenario specs | Yes | Model output; OpenAI grants output rights to the caller. |
| `data/splits/splits.json` | Derived, seeded | Yes | Derived artefact. |
| IRAS guidance pages (30 URLs) | `iras.gov.sg` | **No — gitignored** | Read as reference only. Not redistributed. |
| CFPB Consumer Complaint Database | Accessed through Hugging Face | **No** | Read for register/style only; no complaint text is retained, redistributed, or used for training/evaluation. |
| `models/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` | Hugging Face | Yes | Apache 2.0; upstream licence and attribution are included beside the weights. |

---

## 2. The SOP corpus — authored, not scraped

**No agency publishes its internal SOPs.** Any honest version of this project must
author them, and pretending otherwise would be the more serious misrepresentation.

Each of the 17 SOPs is a **synthetic officer-facing procedure**. Every factual claim
in one traces to a public IRAS URL recorded in that file's `references:` frontmatter —
**30 distinct URLs**, all on `www.iras.gov.sg`.

Three structural guarantees, enforced at load time rather than by convention:

- **Every SOP carries a synthetic banner.** `src/triage/sop/loader.py` raises at
  startup if `synthetic: true` is missing. A corpus that could be mistaken for real
  agency material is the failure mode this guards against.
- **Every SOP must declare at least one reference.** An empty `references:` list is a
  hard load error.
- **Citations are checked, not assumed.** `python scripts/generate_sops.py --check`
  validates that all 148 recorded facts resolve to a declared source. It is a
  Makefile target and part of the normal build.

None of these files reflects internal IRAS material, template, or practice. They are
my reconstruction of what such a procedure would plausibly contain. The
[SOP authoring schema](sop_specs/README.md) is the integration point through which a
real agency could provide its own procedures without changing application code.

### 2.1 How the reference pages were used

`scripts/fetch_reference.py` fetches the registry of public pages into `.scratch/`,
which is **gitignored** (`.gitignore` line 3). The manifest records the URL, fetch date
(2026-09-01), HTTP status and byte count for each.

The fetched HTML exists **only** so that facts written into the SOP specs can be
checked against their source during human review. It is never committed, never
redistributed, and never fed to a model.

Politeness measures: a courtesy rate-limit between requests (`--delay`, default
applied in the fetch loop), a single pass rather than a crawl, and a fixed registry of
~30 named pages rather than link-following. A browser User-Agent is set because the
IRAS site serves a JavaScript navigation shell to unknown agents and returns no
content otherwise — this is to receive the page a human would see, not to evade a
restriction.

`https://www.iras.gov.sg/robots.txt` was checked on **2026-09-03** and returned HTTP
404, so there were no published crawler directives to apply. Absence of a robots file
is not treated as permission: the fixed allowlist, one-second delay, single pass, and
Terms-of-Use analysis below still govern the fetch.

### 2.2 Licensing position, stated plainly

IRAS Terms of Use restrict reproduction of site contents. Read literally, they also
require written permission to hyperlink to an internal page — a provision that reads
as boilerplate and is not observed in practice anywhere on the Singapore web.

**This project does not depend on resolving that question**, because it does not
reproduce site content. The operative principle is that **copyright protects
expression, not facts**. A filing deadline, a relief cap, and a penalty rate are facts
stated in or derived from legislation; they are not anyone's creative expression.

What is committed is my own prose restating those facts, with a citation to where each
came from. What is not committed is any IRAS page, in whole or in part.

**Note on figures.** Relief caps and rates in the SOPs are stated as the public pages
state them. They are a snapshot taken 2026-09-01 and will go stale — a production
version would need effective-date metadata and a re-indexing cadence, which is listed
under future improvements in the README.

---

## 3. Synthetic emails

3,000 emails generated by **GPT-4o** from 116 hand-authored scenario specifications.

### 3.1 Why synthetic

Real citizen correspondence to a tax authority contains NRICs, addresses, income
figures and financial distress. It cannot be obtained lawfully for a take-home
exercise, cannot be ethically used if it could, and no public corpus of Singapore
government email enquiries exists. Synthetic is the only honest option here, and the
question becomes whether it is generated well enough to support a claim.

### 3.2 What makes it defensible

**The generator never sees the label.** It receives a *situation* description
("someone received a message claiming to be from the tax authority asking them to
confirm bank details, and wants to know if it is real"). The class label is attached
afterward from the scenario file. The model cannot write toward a class name, which is
the mechanism that would otherwise plant a giveaway token in every email of a class.

**Three independent axes of variation:**

- *Content* — persona, life situation, and the guidance actually relevant to it.
- *Style* — standard English; imperfect English with typos, run-ons and all-caps;
  lightly Singlish-inflected. Register calibrated against sampled real CFPB complaints
  (read for tone; no text copied).
- *Season* — filing period, estimates, notice-of-assessment period.

Plus an edge-case slice: answerable only from held-out guidance, account-specific
phrasing, and genuine edge cases recalled from prior call-centre experience.

**Model separation.** The generator (OpenAI GPT-4o) differs from the zero-shot
classification baseline and the groundedness judge (both Groq/Qwen). No model in the
evaluation path is ever scored on text it wrote — enforced as an explicit rule in
`config/models.yaml`.

### 3.3 Leakage is tested, not assumed

`python scripts/check_leakage.py` runs seven checks over the committed corpus. All
seven pass on the current one:

0. **Balance** — class counts against the taxonomy (300 per class × 10).
1. **Vocabulary leakage** — a TF-IDF + logistic-regression probe. It should classify
   *well but not perfectly*: a near-perfect score means a giveaway token exists and the
   corpus needs regenerating. Measured accuracy sits in the expected band.
2. **System vocabulary** — no email contains the system's own terms (bucket names,
   SOP ids, class names).
3. **Length as a giveaway** — that message length alone does not carry class signal.
4. **Near-duplicates** — cosine similarity across the corpus.
5. **Boilerplate** — that generated openings and closings do not cluster by class.
6. **Flag confounding** — that a lexical flag is not standing in for a class.

Separately, **splits are grouped by `scenario_id`**, so every variant of a situation
lands in the same split and no paraphrase straddles the train/test boundary. That is
enforced in `scripts/make_splits.py` and verified by zero scenario overlap between
every pair of splits.

### 3.4 Privacy in the generated data

- **All identifiers were generated for the project, not sourced from people.** NRICs
  are checksum-valid so the detector can be tested honestly. The values were not
  checked against official registries, so accidental collision cannot be ruled out.
- Addresses combine public Singapore street and estate names with generated block and
  unit numbers. Phone numbers and postal codes are generated in valid-looking shapes.
- No personal identifier belonging to the author or a known person was used.
- **What was planted is recorded** (`plant_pii` per email), which is what makes scrub
  recall measurable rather than asserted.

### 3.5 Privacy in the pipeline itself

Beyond the data, three properties of the system:

- **Scrubbing happens before any external call.** The classifier and the drafter both
  see placeholder text; real values never leave the machine. Rehydration is local and
  happens after the network call, in exactly one place.
- **No PII in committed results.** `eval/metrics/pii_recall.py` masks missed values at
  the point of capture (`S0433218J` → `S0*****8J`), so the module that measures
  containment cannot itself write an identifier into `eval/results/`.
- **`.env` is gitignored** and `triage.env.key_status()` reports only booleans, never
  key values.

---

## 4. CFPB Consumer Complaint Database

- **Source:** [US Consumer Financial Protection Bureau complaint
  database](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/data-research/consumer-complaints/),
  accessed through a Hugging Face copy during style review.
- **Privacy:** CFPB publishes complaint narratives only after removing personal
  information. No narrative is stored or redistributed by this project.
- **Use:** read to calibrate *register* — how members of the public actually write to
  an institution when frustrated, confused, or in financial difficulty. Sentence
  length, politeness markers, how a complaint opens.
- **Not used for:** training, evaluation, or text reuse. No CFPB text appears in this
  repository. It is American and about consumer finance, so it is a style reference
  only, never a content one.

---

## 5. Model weights

- **`sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`** — Apache 2.0, from Hugging Face.
  Committed to the repo (~88 MB fine-tuned) so a clone yields real weights rather than
  git-lfs pointers. The upstream licence and attribution notice are included beside
  both the base encoder and the fine-tuned derivative.
- Gemini, Groq and OpenAI are accessed by API under their respective terms. No weights
  are redistributed.

---

## 6. What this data does not cover

Recorded here as well as in the README, because it bounds every number reported:

- **116 situations is the binding constraint**, not 3,000 emails. Per-class figures
  rest on ~90 test emails drawn from a handful of situations each, so a class can look
  strong because its few situations happen to be easy.
- **A synthetic ceiling.** This measures performance on a distribution GPT-4o and I
  jointly imagined. It cannot tell you a real inbox looks like this — that is the one
  thing this project cannot check about itself.
- **One agency, one tax type.** Individual income tax only. No corporate tax, GST,
  property tax, or stamp duty.
- **English only**, with Singlish inflection. No Chinese, Malay or Tamil.
- **No attachments, no threads, no forwarded chains.** Every email is a single
  standalone message, which real correspondence often is not.
- **Author-shaped distribution.** The scenario set reflects what I judged
  representative. A real inbox would be shaped by seasonality, campaigns, and
  events nobody anticipated.

The most valuable next data step is not more emails — it is **more situations**, and a
validation-only slice of real anonymised enquiries to test whether the synthetic
situation set resembles the real one.

"""Generate the synthetic email corpus from ``data/scenarios/*.yaml``.

BUILD-TIME ONLY. Uses a paid API. The output is frozen and committed, so a grader
reproducing the results never runs this script and never needs a key.

**The generator is never shown the label.** It receives a *situation* -- a citizen's
circumstance -- plus a persona and a style instruction, and writes an email. The
label is attached afterwards, from the scenario file. This is the corpus's central
anti-leakage property: if the prompt named the class, the emails would carry
vocabulary chosen *because* of the label, and a classifier would learn the
generator's tell rather than the citizen's problem. Reported accuracy would then be
measuring a shortcut.

``scripts/check_leakage.py`` and the EDA notebook test this empirically rather than
trusting the intent: TF-IDF plus logistic regression is fitted on the output, and a
near-perfect score means a giveaway token exists and the corpus is rebuilt.

**Model separation** (``BUILD.md`` S6.4) -- no model may be scored on its own
output:

    generation   OpenAI gpt-4o          <- here; build time, paid
    baseline     Groq qwen3.8-27b        <- must differ from the generator
    drafting     Gemini                  <- runtime, free tier
    judge        Groq qwen3.8-27b        <- must differ from the drafter

Groq appears twice without breaking the rule: the baseline CLASSIFIES EMAILS and
the judge SCORES DRAFTS, so neither is ever scored on its own output. Groq wrote
none of the text it sees in either role.

Usage:
    python scripts/generate_emails.py                 # full run, 3,000 emails
    python scripts/generate_emails.py --limit 12      # smoke test
    python scripts/generate_emails.py --dry-run       # print prompts, call nothing

def load_dotenv(path: Path | None = None) -> None:
    """Read ``.env`` into the environment without adding a dependency.

    Existing environment variables win, so an explicit export still overrides the
    file. ``.env`` is gitignored and must never be committed.

    env_file = path or ROOT / ".env"
    if not env_file.is_file():
        return
    for line in env_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:

        key, _, value = line.partition("=")
        key, value = key.strip(), value.strip().strip("'\"")
        if key and value and key not in os.environ:

# Scenario specs — how the email corpus is generated

Human-authored input to `scripts/generate_emails.py`. A scenario describes a
*situation a citizen is in*, never a class label, and the generator writes the
email from that situation.

This separation keeps the generation prompt independent of the target label and
makes scenario-level train/calibration/test splits possible.

---

## The one rule that matters

**A scenario must never mention its own label, and must never quote SOP text.**

Both are leakage. If a scenario said `class: tax_reliefs` and the generator saw
it, the resulting emails would carry vocabulary chosen *because* of the label, and
the classifier would learn the generator's tell rather than the citizen's problem.
Reported accuracy would then measure a shortcut.

So the pipeline is:

    situation (persona + circumstance)  ->  LLM  ->  email text
    label                               ->  attached AFTERWARDS, never shown

`scripts/check_leakage.py` tests this empirically: a TF-IDF + logistic regression
model is fitted on the generated text. If a bag of words separates the classes
almost perfectly, the emails contain a giveaway and the corpus is rebuilt.

---

## Schema

```yaml
scenario_id: REL-CHILD-001        # <AREA>-<TOPIC>-<NNN>
label: tax_reliefs                # ground truth. NEVER shown to the generator.
source_sops: [SOP-REL-001]        # which SOP(s) answer this; ground truth for
                                  # grounding accuracy

situation: >                      # what the generator sees. No label, no SOP text.
  A parent wants to know whether they can claim something for their
  teenage child who did some part-time work over the holidays.

persona:
  role: employee                  # employee | self_employed | retiree | foreigner | parent
  literacy: standard              # standard | imperfect | singlish
  register: polite                # polite | frustrated | anxious | terse

season: filing                    # filing | estimates | noa | any
                                  # drives received_at, so seasonality is testable

# --- flag ground truth: free, because the scenario declares it ---
computation_requested: false      # does the email demand arithmetic?
account_specific: false           # does it ask about THIS taxpayer's own record?

# --- optional ---
plant_pii: [nric, phone]          # inject fake identifiers for scrub-recall
                                  # measurement. FABRICATED values only.
multi_intent: false               # does it genuinely ask two things?
notes: >                          # why this scenario exists, for the review pass
  Covers the $8,000 child income threshold without asking for a computation.
variants: 6                       # how many emails to generate from this scenario
```

## Fields that are ground truth

These cost nothing to record and are what the evaluation reads. Every one of them
would otherwise require hand-labelling:

| Field | Measures |
|---|---|
| `label` | classification accuracy, macro-F1 |
| `source_sops` | **grounding accuracy** — did the draft use the right SOP? |
| `computation_requested` | the computation flag's precision and recall |
| `account_specific` | the backstop flag's precision and recall |
| `plant_pii` | scrub recall against known planted values |
| `season` | whether performance holds across the tax year |

## Held-out classes

`rental_income` and `foreign_income_dta` have scenarios and labels like any other
class — the classifier must still predict them. What they do not have is an
indexed SOP, so `source_sops` names the held-out file and the router escalates on
`no_supporting_sop`. The emails are ordinary citizen questions; the system simply
has no procedure for them.

## Balance

Equal examples per class, because every class gets its own published number under
per-topic reporting. The edge-case slice is stratified *into* the per-class
allocation rather than added on top, so no class is starved.

**Consequence to remember:** a per-cell figure — say "computation-demanding relief
emails" — rests on roughly 10 test examples. Adequate for a pooled flag metric,
not for a per-class claim about it.

## Conventions

- **Fake identifiers only.** NRICs are fabricated with a valid checksum so the
  validator exercises properly; they belong to nobody.
- **No real personal data**, ever, including the author's own.
- Scenarios are authored to cover the SOP's *scope* and its *not in scope* list,
  so both the answerable and the escalating paths are represented.

# Scenario specs — how the email corpus is generated

Human-authored input to `scripts/generate_emails.py`. A scenario describes a
*situation a citizen is in*, never a class label, and the generator writes the
email from that situation.

This separation keeps the generation prompt independent of the target label and
makes scenario-level train/calibration/test splits possible.

---

## The one rule that matters

**A scenario must never mention its own label, and must never quote SOP text.**

Both are leakage. If a scenario said `class: tax_reliefs` and the generator saw
it, the resulting emails would carry vocabulary chosen *because* of the label, and
the classifier would learn the generator's tell rather than the citizen's problem.
Reported accuracy would then measure a shortcut.

So the pipeline is:

    situation (persona + circumstance)  ->  LLM  ->  email text
    label                               ->  attached AFTERWARDS, never shown

`scripts/check_leakage.py` tests this empirically: a TF-IDF + logistic regression
model is fitted on the generated text. If a bag of words separates the classes
almost perfectly, the emails contain a giveaway and the corpus is rebuilt.

---

## Schema

```yaml
scenario_id: REL-CHILD-001        # <AREA>-<TOPIC>-<NNN>
label: tax_reliefs                # ground truth. NEVER shown to the generator.
source_sops: [SOP-REL-001]        # which SOP(s) answer this; ground truth for
                                  # grounding accuracy

situation: >                      # what the generator sees. No label, no SOP text.
  A parent wants to know whether they can claim something for their
  teenage child who did some part-time work over the holidays.

persona:
  role: employee                  # employee | self_employed | retiree | foreigner | parent
  literacy: standard              # standard | imperfect | singlish
  register: polite                # polite | frustrated | anxious | terse

season: filing                    # filing | estimates | noa | any
                                  # drives received_at, so seasonality is testable

# --- flag ground truth: free, because the scenario declares it ---
computation_requested: false      # does the email demand arithmetic?
account_specific: false           # does it ask about THIS taxpayer's own record?

# --- optional ---
plant_pii: [nric, phone]          # inject fake identifiers for scrub-recall
                                  # measurement. FABRICATED values only.
multi_intent: false               # does it genuinely ask two things?
notes: >                          # why this scenario exists, for the review pass
  Covers the $8,000 child income threshold without asking for a computation.
variants: 6                       # how many emails to generate from this scenario
```

## Fields that are ground truth

These cost nothing to record and are what the evaluation reads. Every one of them
would otherwise require hand-labelling:

| Field | Measures |
|---|---|
| `label` | classification accuracy, macro-F1 |
| `source_sops` | **grounding accuracy** — did the draft use the right SOP? |
| `computation_requested` | the computation flag's precision and recall |
| `account_specific` | the backstop flag's precision and recall |
| `plant_pii` | scrub recall against known planted values |
| `season` | whether performance holds across the tax year |

## Held-out classes

`rental_income` and `foreign_income_dta` have scenarios and labels like any other
class — the classifier must still predict them. What they do not have is an
indexed SOP, so `source_sops` names the held-out file and the router escalates on
`no_supporting_sop`. The emails are ordinary citizen questions; the system simply
has no procedure for them.

## Balance

Equal examples per class, because every class gets its own published number under
per-topic reporting. The edge-case slice is stratified *into* the per-class
allocation rather than added on top, so no class is starved.

**Consequence to remember:** a per-cell figure — say "computation-demanding relief
emails" — rests on roughly 10 test examples. Adequate for a pooled flag metric,
not for a per-class claim about it.

## Conventions

- **Fake identifiers only.** NRICs are fabricated with a valid checksum so the
  validator exercises properly; they belong to nobody.
- **No real personal data**, ever, including the author's own.
- Scenarios are authored to cover the SOP's *scope* and its *not in scope* list,
  so both the answerable and the escalating paths are represented.

# Scenario specs — how the email corpus is generated

Human-authored input to `scripts/generate_emails.py`. A scenario describes a
*situation a citizen is in*, never a class label, and the generator writes the
email from that situation.

This separation keeps the generation prompt independent of the target label and
makes scenario-level train/calibration/test splits possible.

---

## The one rule that matters

**A scenario must never mention its own label, and must never quote SOP text.**

Both are leakage. If a scenario said `class: tax_reliefs` and the generator saw
it, the resulting emails would carry vocabulary chosen *because* of the label, and
the classifier would learn the generator's tell rather than the citizen's problem.
Reported accuracy would then measure a shortcut.

So the pipeline is:

    situation (persona + circumstance)  ->  LLM  ->  email text
    label                               ->  attached AFTERWARDS, never shown

`scripts/check_leakage.py` tests this empirically: a TF-IDF + logistic regression
model is fitted on the generated text. If a bag of words separates the classes
almost perfectly, the emails contain a giveaway and the corpus is rebuilt.

---

## Schema

```yaml
scenario_id: REL-CHILD-001        # <AREA>-<TOPIC>-<NNN>
label: tax_reliefs                # ground truth. NEVER shown to the generator.
source_sops: [SOP-REL-001]        # which SOP(s) answer this; ground truth for
                                  # grounding accuracy

situation: >                      # what the generator sees. No label, no SOP text.
  A parent wants to know whether they can claim something for their
  teenage child who did some part-time work over the holidays.

persona:
  role: employee                  # employee | self_employed | retiree | foreigner | parent
  literacy: standard              # standard | imperfect | singlish
  register: polite                # polite | frustrated | anxious | terse

season: filing                    # filing | estimates | noa | any
                                  # drives received_at, so seasonality is testable

# --- flag ground truth: free, because the scenario declares it ---
computation_requested: false      # does the email demand arithmetic?
account_specific: false           # does it ask about THIS taxpayer's own record?

# --- optional ---
plant_pii: [nric, phone]          # inject fake identifiers for scrub-recall
                                  # measurement. FABRICATED values only.
multi_intent: false               # does it genuinely ask two things?
notes: >                          # why this scenario exists, for the review pass
  Covers the $8,000 child income threshold without asking for a computation.
variants: 6                       # how many emails to generate from this scenario
```

| `computation_requested` | the computation flag's precision and recall |
| `account_specific` | the backstop flag's precision and recall |
| `plant_pii` | scrub recall against known planted values |
| `season` | whether performance holds across the tax year |

## Held-out classes

`rental_income` and `foreign_income_dta` have scenarios and labels like any other
class — the classifier must still predict them. What they do not have is an
indexed SOP, so `source_sops` names the held-out file and the router escalates on
`no_supporting_sop`. The emails are ordinary citizen questions; the system simply
has no procedure for them.

## Balance

**Consequence to remember:** a per-cell figure — say "computation-demanding relief

*** Add File: eval/HUMAN_EVAL.md
+# Human evaluation protocol
+
+This protocol measures successful draft quality and checks the LLM groundedness
+judge against independent human review. Humans are the reference. See the
+[current status](results/HUMAN_EVAL_REPORT.md).
+
+## Sample and blinding
+
+- \`eval/run_eval.py\` takes a seeded random sample without replacement from automated routes.
+- Provider failures count toward drafting availability but have no draft to review.
+- Reviewers see the scrubbed email, supplied SOPs, and redacted draft.
+- Reviewer sheets hide the judge verdict, classifier output, confidence, labels, scenario ID, and source email ID.
+- Do not inspect \`manifest.json\` or \`drafts.json\` while rating.
+- One reviewer rates every successful draft.
+- A second reviewer rates \`max(20, 30%)\` items, capped at the sample size.
+
+Use anonymous reviewer IDs and do not commit names or email addresses.
+
+## Rubric
+
+Use only these values:
+
+| Field | Values | Pass rule |
+|---|---|---|
+| \`groundedness\` | \`GROUNDED\`, \`UNGROUNDED\`, \`UNSURE\` | Every factual claim is supported by an SOP or clearly attributed to the citizen |
+| \`correct_next_step\` | \`PASS\`, \`FAIL\`, \`UNSURE\` | The action or destination answers the request and follows the SOP |
+| \`safety_privacy\` | \`PASS\`, \`FAIL\`, \`UNSURE\` | No invented identifier, sensitive disclosure, unsafe instruction, or unsupported promise |
+| \`completeness\` | \`PASS\`, \`FAIL\`, \`UNSURE\` | All material, supported parts and essential SOP steps are covered |
+| \`tone\` | \`PASS\`, \`FAIL\`, \`UNSURE\` | Clear, respectful, neutral, and free of false certainty |
+| \`overall_acceptability\` | \`ACCEPT\`, \`REJECT\`, \`UNSURE\` | An officer could send it after proofreading without a substantive correction |
+
+\`UNGROUNDED\` or \`safety_privacy=FAIL\` requires \`REJECT\`. Explain every failure,
+rejection, and \`UNSURE\` rating in \`review_notes\`, citing the sentence and SOP
+evidence. Do not penalise harmless style preferences.
+
+## Procedure
+
+1. Run the live drafting evaluation so \`eval/results/drafts.json\` exists.
+2. Create blinded sheets:
+
+\`\`\`bash
+python eval/human_review.py prepare --reviewer-id reviewer_a --output eval/human_review/reviewer_a.csv
+python eval/human_review.py prepare --reviewer-id reviewer_b --overlap-only --output eval/human_review/reviewer_b.csv

# Human evaluation protocol

This protocol evaluates the quality of successful model-written drafts and validates
the LLM groundedness judge against independent human review. Humans are the reference;
the judge is a scalable evaluation aid, not a substitute for review.

## Sample and evidence

`eval/run_eval.py` takes a deterministic simple random sample without replacement
from all actions automated at the frozen operating point. Failed provider calls are
reported as drafting availability failures and have no text to review. Each successful
sampled draft is reviewed against exactly three artefacts:

1. the citizen correspondence after local PII scrubbing;
2. every SOP supplied to the drafter; and
3. the redacted draft.

The reviewer sheet deliberately omits the LLM judge verdict, classifier prediction,
confidence, true label, scenario identifier, and original email identifier. Do not
open `manifest.json` or `drafts.json` while rating.

One primary reviewer rates every successful draft. A second reviewer independently
rates the manifest's fixed overlap subset: the greater of 20 items or 30% of the
sample, capped at the sample size. Resolve every disagreement and every `UNSURE` with
a separate adjudication row. Use anonymous reviewer IDs such as `reviewer_a`; do not
commit names or email addresses.

## Rubric

Use only the capitalised values shown below.

| Field | Allowed values | Decision rule |
|---|---|---|
| `groundedness` | `GROUNDED`, `UNGROUNDED`, `UNSURE` | Every factual claim about rules, amounts, eligibility, deadlines, process, or agency action is supported by an SOP or clearly attributed to the citizen. |
| `correct_next_step` | `PASS`, `FAIL`, `UNSURE` | The proposed action or destination addresses the correspondence and is allowed by the SOP. |
| `safety_privacy` | `PASS`, `FAIL`, `UNSURE` | No invented identifier, sensitive disclosure, unsafe instruction, or unsupported commitment appears. Placeholders such as `[NRIC_1]` are intentional redactions. |
| `completeness` | `PASS`, `FAIL`, `UNSURE` | The draft answers the material supported parts without omitting an essential SOP step. |
| `tone` | `PASS`, `FAIL`, `UNSURE` | Clear, respectful, neutral public-service language; no blame, pressure, or false certainty. |
| `overall_acceptability` | `ACCEPT`, `REJECT`, `UNSURE` | Could an officer send this after ordinary proofreading, without correcting substance? |

An `UNGROUNDED` or `safety_privacy=FAIL` rating is a hard rejection. Explain every
failure, rejection, or unsure decision in `review_notes`, naming the exact sentence
and relevant SOP evidence. Do not penalise harmless wording preferences.

## Procedure

After a live draft/judge run has written `eval/results/drafts.json`, create the two
blinded sheets:

```powershell
python eval/human_review.py prepare `
  --reviewer-id reviewer_a `
  --output eval/human_review/reviewer_a.csv

python eval/human_review.py prepare `
  --reviewer-id reviewer_b `
  --overlap-only `
  --output eval/human_review/reviewer_b.csv
```

Review independently. If the scoring command reports unresolved fields, copy those
items into a third sheet with `reviewer_id=adjudicator`, review the underlying evidence
without treating either reviewer as authoritative, and pass that file with
`--adjudication`.

```powershell
python eval/human_review.py score `
  --ratings eval/human_review/reviewer_a.csv eval/human_review/reviewer_b.csv `
  --adjudication eval/human_review/adjudicated.csv
```

The command writes both the machine-readable
`eval/results/judge_human_agreement.json` and the README-facing
`eval/results/HUMAN_EVAL_REPORT.md`. It refuses malformed categories, unexplained
failures, unknown item IDs, modified evidence, and inconsistent hard-failure
acceptance. An incomplete annotation set remains explicitly `status: incomplete` in
both reports.

## Reported quantities

- Human pass/acceptance rates with 95% Wilson intervals.
- Human-human raw agreement and Cohen's kappa on the overlap subset.
- Judge-human raw agreement, Cohen's kappa, and confusion matrix.
- Judge recall and precision for human-identified `UNGROUNDED` drafts.
- Judge-human agreement split between auto-replies and redirects.
- Annotation, judge, double-review, and unresolved-item coverage.

Kappa is reported as undefined when one or both raters use only one class. If humans
identify no ungrounded draft, judge recall is also undefined; high agreement alone
must not be used to claim the judge catches hallucinations. The results validate only
this frozen prompt, model, sample, and synthetic evaluation setting.

# SOP-ESC-001 — Account-specific enquiries
#
# Class: account_specific. Bucket: requires_account_lookup — ALWAYS ESCALATES.
#
# `auto_reply_permitted: false` is what puts this class in an always-escalate
# bucket. The BUCKET map is derived from that field, so escalation policy lives in
# the corpus rather than in code.
#
# KNOWN SIMPLIFICATION. "Generic versus my case" genuinely
# cuts across every topic and structurally belongs as a flag, not a class: "what
# is the filing deadline" and "why was MY deduction reversed" differ by a
# possessive, not by subject matter. It is kept as a class for the prototype
# because a flag needs a second detector and the lexical signal is weak.
#
# Consequence accepted in review: this class will be confused with whichever topic
# the email is about, because topical vocabulary dominates the one-or-two-token
# possessive signal — and the confusion lands on the unsafe side, since a missed
# account_specific means auto-drafting about a real taxpayer's account. A lexical
# `account_specific` BACKSTOP FLAG is therefore specified below, mirroring
# `computation_requested`: it forces escalation on strong possessive signals
# regardless of the predicted class. Measured, not assumed — report its precision
# and recall alongside the computation flag.

sop_id: SOP-ESC-001
title: Account-specific enquiries
version: "1.0"
effective_date: 2026-01-01
supersedes: null
applies_to_ya: [2025, 2026]
intents: [account_specific]
indexed: true
owner_queue: IIT-General          # INVENTED — not a real IRAS queue
handling_target: 3_working_days   # ILLUSTRATIVE — not a real IRAS SLA
auto_reply_permitted: false       # -> bucket: requires_account_lookup
escalate_if:
  - account_specific

# Lexical backstop, applied AFTER the bucket rollup alongside `computation_requested`.
# Detection is a rule set, not a model: auditable, free, and testable.
backstop_flag:
  name: account_specific_signal
  rationale: >
    Converts a known taxonomy compromise into a measured safety net. Fires
    independently of the predicted class and forces escalation.
  patterns:
STALE: <REPOSITORY>\config\taxonomy.yaml does not match the corpus.
Run: python scripts/derive_taxonomy.py
EXIT=1

 # Calibrated Triage for Citizen Correspondence
 
-A triage agent for a tax authority's individual-income-tax inbox. It reads a
-citizen's email, classifies the intent, looks up the governing internal procedure,
-and either drafts a grounded reply or escalates to an officer with a stated reason.
-
-**The contribution is not the drafting. It is knowing when not to draft.**
-
-> **Demo video:** _[URL to be added before submission]_
-
----
-
-## 1. The problem
-
-An agency inbox is not one problem. It is a mixture of questions that a published
-FAQ already answers, questions that require reading a specific taxpayer's record,
-and questions where a wrong answer causes real harm — a citizen mid-fraud, or one
-who cannot pay.
-
-The naive framing is "use an LLM to answer citizen emails". That framing fails on
-the only question an agency actually has, which is not *can it draft?* but:
-
-> **What share of this inbox can I safely automate, and at what error rate?**
-
-That is a coverage/risk trade-off, and it is a curve rather than a number. A system
-that answers 100% of emails at 15% error is unusable in a public-sector context; one
-that answers 35% at 9% error, and hands the rest to a human *with a reason attached*,
-is deployable. This project is built around producing and defending that curve.
-
-This is Annex A sketch 12 (triage agent for citizen emails), taken deliberately at
-its hardest reading: **calibrated confidence and clean human escalation**, not
-autocomplete for officers.
-
----
-
-## 2. What it does
-
-```
-  mock inbox (JSON)
-        |
-        v
-  1. PII SCRUB ......... local regex + gazetteer; placeholders substituted
-        |                BEFORE any external call
-        v
-  2. CLASSIFIER ........ MiniLM-L6, fine-tuned, 10 classes, local CPU
-        |
-        v
-  3. BUCKET ROLLUP ..... 10 classes -> 5 routing buckets
-        |
-        v
-  4. CALIBRATION ....... temperature scaling on the bucket distribution
-        |
-        v
-  5. SOP LOOKUP ........ CLASS_TO_SOPS[class] from SOP frontmatter
-        |                no vector search, no embeddings
-        v
-  6. ROUTER ............ decide(bucket, calibrated confidence, flags)
-        |
-        +---> AUTO-REPLY .... Gemini, grounded in the retrieved SOP
-        +---> REDIRECT ...... out-of-scope, still SOP-grounded
-        +---> HUMAN QUEUE ... with an escalation reason
+A prototype for triaging a tax authority's individual-income-tax inbox. It removes
+personal data locally, classifies each email, retrieves the relevant synthetic SOP,
+and either prepares a grounded response or sends the item to an officer with a clear
+reason.
+
+**The main contribution is not drafting. It is knowing when not to draft.**
+
+> **Demo video (3-5 minutes): TODO - add the URL before submission.**
+
+## What it does
+
+```text
+email
+  -> scrub PII locally
+  -> classify into 1 of 10 intents with a fine-tuned MiniLM-L6 model
+  -> roll up to 1 of 5 routing buckets and calibrate confidence
+  -> retrieve SOPs by an exact class-to-SOP mapping
+  -> route
+       -> auto-reply or redirect: ask Gemini for an SOP-grounded draft
+       -> officer queue: attach the SOP and an escalation reason
 ```
 
-Orchestrated in **LangGraph**. The execution path is a declared graph rather than an
-implicit consequence of control flow, so "what happened to this email" is answerable
-by reading the edges.
-

-## 3. Why this shape
-
-**Routing, not autonomy.** The agent has one decision to make and no tools to call.
-An autonomous pattern would add failure modes to the one path in the system that must
-not have any. Constrained patterns whose path is traceable end to end are the right
-shape for high-stakes public-sector workflows.
+The workflow is a LangGraph graph. An escalated email has no graph edge to the
+drafting node, so the safety gate is structural. At runtime, classification,
+calibration, SOP retrieval, and routing are local. Only eligible drafting uses an
+external API, and it receives scrubbed text.
 
-**An encoder, not an LLM, for classification.** This is the load-bearing model choice
-and it is justified on operational grounds, measured rather than asserted (§6.3):
+The officer-facing Streamlit app presents an inbox, a processing view, and a results
+workspace with editable drafts, escalation reasons, supporting SOPs, and a
+risk-coverage chart. It never sends an email.
 
-- **Calibratable confidence.** A softmax over a linear head is native to the
-  architecture. Extracting a distribution from a text-generating model needs logprobs
-  (not always exposed) or repeated sampling — and self-consistency at *k* samples can
-  only ever express multiples of 1/*k*. Measured: **30 distinct confidence values vs 3.**
-  When the threshold *is* the product, that resolution cap is disqualifying.
-- **Latency and cost.** 0.67 s/email local CPU vs 10.6 s/email via API.
-- **Data sensitivity.** The classifier never leaves the machine. Only the drafter
-  makes an external call, and only ever on scrubbed text.
-- **Deployment size.** MiniLM-L6 at ~88 MB commits to plain git under GitHub's 100 MB
-  limit, so a grader cloning this repo gets real weights, not LFS pointers.

-### 4.2 Synthetic emails, and the defence for them
-
-3,000 emails from **116 authored scenarios**, generated by GPT-4o. Real citizen
-correspondence cannot ethically be used, and no public corpus of Singapore government
-email enquiries exists.
-
-The generation is structured to avoid the failure mode that makes synthetic data
-worthless — a model learning the generator's tells rather than the intent:
-
-- **The generator never sees the label.** It receives a *situation* description. The
-  label is attached afterward from the scenario file. It cannot write toward a class name.
-- **Three independent axes of variation:** content (persona + life situation), style
-  (standard English, imperfect English with typos and all-caps, lightly Singlish-inflected),
-  and season (filing / estimates / NOA periods).
-- **Separation of models.** The generator (GPT-4o) differs from the zero-shot baseline
-  and the judge (Groq/Qwen). No model in the evaluation path scores its own output.
-- **Fake NRICs only**, checksum-valid but not issued.
-
-`scripts/check_leakage.py` tests this rather than assuming it: a TF-IDF + logistic
-regression probe should be *able* to classify but not perfectly (a near-perfect score
-means a giveaway token exists). It also checks that no email contains the system's
-own vocabulary.
-

-
-Stated plainly, because it bounds every number below:
-
-- **Situation breadth is the binding constraint, not size.** 3,000 emails come from
-  116 situations, ~26 variants each. Per-class figures rest on ~90 test emails drawn
-  from a handful of situations, so a class can look strong because its few situations
-  are easy.
-- **Synthetic ceiling.** This measures performance on a distribution the author and
-  GPT-4o jointly imagined. It cannot tell you the real inbox looks like this.
-- Single agency, single tax type, English-only (with Singlish inflection, not Chinese/
-  Malay/Tamil).
-- Splits are **grouped by scenario** — every variant of a situation lands in the same
-  split, so the model is asked to generalise to unseen *situations*, not unseen
-  paraphrases. This is stricter than a random split and lowers the headline numbers.

-## 5. Evaluation methodology, and why
-
-**Benchmarking + ablation + a bounded LLM-as-judge.** Three methods because they
-answer different questions, and the primary metric is a curve, not a score.
-
-**5.1 Risk–coverage, reported per topic.** The headline. Coverage is the share acted
-on without a human (auto-replies *and* redirects — under a no-back-door policy a clean
-redirect is the correct outcome, not a failure). Risk is the share of those automated
-actions that were wrong. The curve is swept by scaling every threshold through 37
-multipliers **using the real router**, not a reimplementation, so the published curve
-cannot drift from the system it describes.
-
-Reported **per topic, never as one inbox figure**: an aggregate depends on the class
-volume mix, which is unpublished and seasonal. Per-topic coverage is composable — an
-agency multiplies through its own mix.
-
-**5.2 Calibration.** ECE plus reliability diagrams, before and after temperature
-scaling. Fitted on a dedicated `calibration` split, reported on `test`. Fitting and
-reporting on the same data would make the headline meaningless.
-
-**5.3 Ablations.** Three, each isolating one design claim: does calibration change any
-*decision* or only the ECE; do per-bucket thresholds beat one global number; does
-scrubbing PII cost accuracy.
-
-**5.4 Comparison.** Fine-tuned encoder vs LLM zero-shot with self-consistency, on the
-same stratified sample with a **fixed label set** for both (deriving the label set from
-the data makes the two macro-F1 figures averages over different denominators — a
-0.11–0.22 discrepancy on identical predictions).
-
-**5.5 LLM-as-judge — declared incomplete.** A Groq-hosted judge scores draft
-groundedness, deliberately a different model family from the drafter. BUILD.md commits
-to reporting judge–human agreement, because agreement is what makes an LLM judge
-defensible rather than decorative. **That agreement figure has not been computed, so
-no groundedness number is claimed here.** See §8.

+## Results
+
+Offline results use the 877-email test split and seed 42.
+
+| Metric | Result |
+|---|---:|
+| Macro-F1, 10 classes | **0.859** (95% interval 0.769-0.923) |
+| Macro-F1, 5 buckets | 0.917 (0.862-0.971) |
+| Bucket accuracy | 0.928 (0.874-0.976) |
+| Must-escalate recall | **1.000** (456/456) |
+| Unsafe must-escalate automations | **0/456** |
+| Coverage at the frozen operating point | **11.6%** (102/877) |
+| Risk among automated actions | **1.0%** (1/102; interval 0.0%-3.7%) |

+| Area under the risk-coverage curve | 0.0513 |
+
+The aggregate coverage figure describes this deliberately balanced benchmark, not a
+production inbox. Real coverage depends on the agency's seasonal topic mix.
+
+The ablations are deliberately modest: calibration changed ECE from 0.1507 to 0.1502
+and did not change AURC; per-bucket thresholds improved AURC from 0.0584 to 0.0513;
+and PII scrubbing changed class macro-F1 by -0.0011. The near-identity fitted
+temperature (`T=0.998`) is a negative result, not a claimed win.
+
+## Limitations
+
+- The benchmark contains 3,000 emails but only 116 underlying situations. Wide
+  scenario-bootstrap intervals and the calibration/test performance gap show that
+  situation breadth is the binding constraint.
+- Synthetic performance does not establish performance on a real inbox. The next
+  evidence needed is a validation-only slice of real, lawfully anonymised enquiries.
+- PII recall covers values deliberately planted by the generator, not every form a
+  citizen might write. Regex and gazetteer rules should eventually be replaced or
+  supplemented by an offline NER model.
+- The lexical scam flag reached 95.2% recall on the test split, but indirect reports
+  remain hard to detect. A bounded second-pass model is a candidate improvement.
+- Drafting groundedness and judge-human agreement remain unreported because the live
+  sample and human ratings are incomplete.
+- The corpus covers one tax type, English-only single-message emails, synthetic SOPs,
+  and no attachments or conversation threads.
+- Free-tier model identifiers and quotas can change. Failures are surfaced safely,
+  but drafting availability must be monitored separately from routing quality.
+
+## Deployment considerations
+
+The target user is a correspondence officer working inside an agency environment,
+not a citizen. The classifier and routing policy can run on an on-premise CPU; only
+scrubbed text from routes eligible for drafting crosses the boundary to Gemini. The
+fine-tuned checkpoint is 87.4 MB, while the repository carries roughly 175 MB across
+the base and fine-tuned weight copies. Measured sequential classification was about
+0.67 seconds per email, or roughly 19 single-core hours per 100,000 messages before
+batching improvements. If a production inbox matched the balanced benchmark, the
+11.6% operating coverage would imply about 11,600 drafting calls per 100,000 emails;
+the real cost must be recalculated from the agency's topic mix and provider pricing.
+
+Post-deployment monitoring should track bucket-level accuracy and calibration,
+officer overrides, escalation-reason mix, route-specific coverage and risk, PII
+leakage tests, and drafting availability. The clearest deployment risk is seasonal
+distribution shift: filing, assessment, and payment periods change both volume and
+topic mix. Confidence may then stop matching correctness even when aggregate
+accuracy looks stable. Mitigations are rolling labelled samples, seasonal
+recalibration, alerts on confidence distributions and override rates, and a policy
+that keeps high-consequence or unsupported cases outside automated drafting.
+
+## Development narrative
+
+The taxonomy began with 12 classes and was reduced to 10 after evaluation.
+`oos_business_tax` and `oos_other_agency` were merged because they have the same
+action and were not separable reliably. `account_specific` became a cross-topic flag
+because it describes a property of an enquiry, not its subject.
+
+Several strategies were discarded after testing: vector search added uncertainty to
+a 17-document hand-indexed corpus; isotonic calibration was too flexible for 646
+calibration examples; and broad address matching removed ordinary language without
+improving useful recall. Adversarial tests also found ordering and punctuation bugs in
+the PII rules, a stale escalation metric, and a citation-parser error. Provider model
+retirements reinforced the decision to record model identifiers and to fail visibly
+into the officer queue.
+
+## Coding-agent usage
+
+Claude Code (Claude Opus) supported implementation, test creation, and adversarial
+audits. Codex was used to audit this README against the repository and assessment
+brief, simplify it, and verify the documented commands. Agent output was reviewed by
+the author, and numerical claims were checked against committed evaluation artifacts
+or reproduced at the command line.
+
+Coding-agent records belong in [`AI assistant logs/`](AI%20assistant%20logs/). The
+repository currently contains a consolidated brainstorm log only. The remaining raw
+session and chat logs still need to be reviewed for secrets and personal data, then
+added before submission.

+## Design decisions
 
-## Why specs rather than prose
+### The corpus controls routing
 
-Every factual claim in an SOP must trace to a public IRAS URL (`sop_design.md`
-S8.2). A spec makes that structural rather than aspirational: each fact is a
-record carrying its own `source`, and the generator refuses to render a fact
-without one. The traceability guarantee is therefore enforced by the build, not
-by a promise in the README.
+Each SOP declares the intents it supports, whether automated replies are permitted,
+and which conditions require escalation. At startup the application inverts those
+fields into the class-to-SOP and class-to-bucket mappings. Routing policy therefore
+lives in the corpus rather than in a duplicate table in application code.
 
----
+The runtime uses exact lookup instead of vector search. With 17 authored documents
+and a closed 10-class taxonomy, the mapping is complete, deterministic, and easy to
+audit. A similarity model would add a failure threshold directly before the
+escalation decision without solving an ambiguity present in this corpus.
 
-## Schema
+### Holdouts test missing knowledge
+
+Fourteen SOPs are indexed and three are deliberately held out:
+
+- `SOP-INC-001` and `SOP-INC-002` remove all indexed support for
+  `rental_income` and `foreign_income_dta`. The router derives
+  `no_supporting_sop` from the empty lookup and escalates.
+- `SOP-REL-005` removes the overall personal-relief cap from an otherwise
+  supported class. This creates a partial-knowledge case without making all tax
+  relief questions unanswerable.
+
+The agent never computes a citizen's tax or relief amount. Computation requests are
+flagged and escalated because caps, ordering rules, and interacting reliefs cannot be
+handled safely from a short prose procedure.
+
+### The SOPs are synthetic
+
+The files are author-written procedures based only on public IRAS guidance. Every
+fact in a spec names a source handle, every handle resolves to a URL declared in the
+same spec, and every rendered document carries a synthetic banner. Invented queue
+names and handling targets are marked as illustrative.
+
+Approved phrasing is rendered into each SOP as grounded source material. Live replies
+are still produced only by the configured drafter; the application has no local
+template fallback.

# Human evaluation protocol

This protocol evaluates the quality of successful model-written drafts and validates
the LLM groundedness judge against independent human review. Humans are the reference;
the judge is a scalable evaluation aid, not a substitute for review.

## Sample and evidence

`eval/run_eval.py` takes a deterministic simple random sample without replacement
from all actions automated at the frozen operating point. Failed provider calls are
reported as drafting availability failures and have no text to review. Each successful
sampled draft is reviewed against exactly three artefacts:

1. the citizen correspondence after local PII scrubbing;
2. every SOP supplied to the drafter; and
3. the redacted draft.

The reviewer sheet deliberately omits the LLM judge verdict, classifier prediction,
confidence, true label, scenario identifier, and original email identifier. Do not
open `manifest.json` or `drafts.json` while rating.

One primary reviewer rates every successful draft. A second reviewer independently
rates the manifest's fixed overlap subset: the greater of 20 items or 30% of the
sample, capped at the sample size. Resolve every disagreement and every `UNSURE` with
a separate adjudication row. Use anonymous reviewer IDs such as `reviewer_a`; do not
commit names or email addresses.

## Rubric

Use only the capitalised values shown below.

| Field | Allowed values | Decision rule |
|---|---|---|
| `groundedness` | `GROUNDED`, `UNGROUNDED`, `UNSURE` | Every factual claim about rules, amounts, eligibility, deadlines, process, or agency action is supported by an SOP or clearly attributed to the citizen. |
| `correct_next_step` | `PASS`, `FAIL`, `UNSURE` | The proposed action or destination addresses the correspondence and is allowed by the SOP. |
| `safety_privacy` | `PASS`, `FAIL`, `UNSURE` | No invented identifier, sensitive disclosure, unsafe instruction, or unsupported commitment appears. Placeholders such as `[NRIC_1]` are intentional redactions. |
| `completeness` | `PASS`, `FAIL`, `UNSURE` | The draft answers the material supported parts without omitting an essential SOP step. |
| `tone` | `PASS`, `FAIL`, `UNSURE` | Clear, respectful, neutral public-service language; no blame, pressure, or false certainty. |
| `overall_acceptability` | `ACCEPT`, `REJECT`, `UNSURE` | Could an officer send this after ordinary proofreading, without correcting substance? |

An `UNGROUNDED` or `safety_privacy=FAIL` rating is a hard rejection. Explain every
failure, rejection, or unsure decision in `review_notes`, naming the exact sentence
and relevant SOP evidence. Do not penalise harmless wording preferences.

## Procedure

After a live draft/judge run has written `eval/results/drafts.json`, create the two
blinded sheets:

```powershell
python eval/human_review.py prepare `
  --reviewer-id reviewer_a `
  --output eval/human_review/reviewer_a.csv

python eval/human_review.py prepare `
  --reviewer-id reviewer_b `
  --overlap-only `
  --output eval/human_review/reviewer_b.csv
```

Review independently. If the scoring command reports unresolved fields, copy those
items into a third sheet with `reviewer_id=adjudicator`, review the underlying evidence
without treating either reviewer as authoritative, and pass that file with
`--adjudication`.

```powershell
python eval/human_review.py score `
  --ratings eval/human_review/reviewer_a.csv eval/human_review/reviewer_b.csv `
  --adjudication eval/human_review/adjudicated.csv
```

The command writes both the machine-readable
`eval/results/judge_human_agreement.json` and the README-facing
`eval/results/HUMAN_EVAL_REPORT.md`. It refuses malformed categories, unexplained
failures, unknown item IDs, modified evidence, and inconsistent hard-failure
acceptance. An incomplete annotation set remains explicitly `status: incomplete` in
both reports.

## Reported quantities

- Human pass/acceptance rates with 95% Wilson intervals.
- Human-human raw agreement and Cohen's kappa on the overlap subset.
- Judge-human raw agreement, Cohen's kappa, and confusion matrix.
- Judge recall and precision for human-identified `UNGROUNDED` drafts.
- Judge-human agreement split between auto-replies and redirects.
- Annotation, judge, double-review, and unresolved-item coverage.

Kappa is reported as undefined when one or both raters use only one class. If humans
identify no ungrounded draft, judge recall is also undefined; high agreement alone
must not be used to claim the judge catches hallucinations. The results validate only
this frozen prompt, model, sample, and synthetic evaluation setting.

# Human draft evaluation and judge agreement

**Status: NOT RUN**

1. complete the live drafting and LLM-judge sample;
2. generate the blinded reviewer forms;
3. collect one full independent review and the fixed second-review overlap;
4. adjudicate disagreements and `UNSURE` ratings; and

The final report will contain human pass rates with 95% Wilson intervals,

See the full [`eval/HUMAN_EVAL.md`](../HUMAN_EVAL.md) protocol and the current

# Scenario specs — how the email corpus is generated

Human-authored input to `scripts/generate_emails.py`. A scenario describes a
*situation a citizen is in*, never a class label, and the generator writes the
email from that situation.

This separation keeps the generation prompt independent of the target label and
makes scenario-level train/calibration/test splits possible.

---

## The one rule that matters

**A scenario must never mention its own label, and must never quote SOP text.**

Both are leakage. If a scenario said `class: tax_reliefs` and the generator saw
it, the resulting emails would carry vocabulary chosen *because* of the label, and
the classifier would learn the generator's tell rather than the citizen's problem.
Reported accuracy would then measure a shortcut.

So the pipeline is:

    situation (persona + circumstance)  ->  LLM  ->  email text
    label                               ->  attached AFTERWARDS, never shown

`scripts/check_leakage.py` tests this empirically: a TF-IDF + logistic regression
model is fitted on the generated text. If a bag of words separates the classes
almost perfectly, the emails contain a giveaway and the corpus is rebuilt.

---

## Schema

```yaml
scenario_id: REL-CHILD-001        # <AREA>-<TOPIC>-<NNN>
label: tax_reliefs                # ground truth. NEVER shown to the generator.
source_sops: [SOP-REL-001]        # which SOP(s) answer this; ground truth for
                                  # grounding accuracy

situation: >                      # what the generator sees. No label, no SOP text.
  A parent wants to know whether they can claim something for their
  teenage child who did some part-time work over the holidays.

persona:
  role: employee                  # employee | self_employed | retiree | foreigner | parent
  literacy: standard              # standard | imperfect | singlish
  register: polite                # polite | frustrated | anxious | terse

season: filing                    # filing | estimates | noa | any
                                  # drives received_at, so seasonality is testable

# --- flag ground truth: free, because the scenario declares it ---
computation_requested: false      # does the email demand arithmetic?
account_specific: false           # does it ask about THIS taxpayer's own record?

# --- optional ---
plant_pii: [nric, phone]          # inject fake identifiers for scrub-recall
                                  # measurement. FABRICATED values only.
multi_intent: false               # does it genuinely ask two things?
notes: >                          # why this scenario exists, for the review pass
  Covers the $8,000 child income threshold without asking for a computation.
variants: 6                       # how many emails to generate from this scenario
```

## Fields that are ground truth

These cost nothing to record and are what the evaluation reads. Every one of them
would otherwise require hand-labelling:

| Field | Measures |
|---|---|
| `label` | classification accuracy, macro-F1 |
| `source_sops` | **grounding accuracy** — did the draft use the right SOP? |
| `computation_requested` | the computation flag's precision and recall |
| `account_specific` | the backstop flag's precision and recall |
| `plant_pii` | scrub recall against known planted values |
| `season` | whether performance holds across the tax year |

## Held-out classes

`rental_income` and `foreign_income_dta` have scenarios and labels like any other
class — the classifier must still predict them. What they do not have is an
indexed SOP, so `source_sops` names the held-out file and the router escalates on
`no_supporting_sop`. The emails are ordinary citizen questions; the system simply
has no procedure for them.

## Balance

Equal examples per class, because every class gets its own published number under
per-topic reporting. The edge-case slice is stratified *into* the per-class
allocation rather than added on top, so no class is starved.

**Consequence to remember:** a per-cell figure — say "computation-demanding relief
emails" — rests on roughly 10 test examples. Adequate for a pooled flag metric,
not for a per-class claim about it.

## Conventions

- **Fake identifiers only.** NRICs are fabricated with a valid checksum so the
  validator exercises properly; they belong to nobody.
- **No real personal data**, ever, including the author's own.
- Scenarios are authored to cover the SOP's *scope* and its *not in scope* list,
  so both the answerable and the escalating paths are represented.

# SOP schema and corpus design

`data/sop_specs/*.yaml` is the human-authored source of truth for the synthetic
officer procedures. `scripts/generate_sops.py` validates those specs and renders
the Markdown corpus in `data/sop/`; generated SOPs should not be edited directly.

For source provenance, licensing, and privacy details, see
[Data sources](../SOURCES.md).

## Design decisions

### The corpus controls routing

Each SOP declares the intents it supports, whether automated replies are permitted,
and which conditions require escalation. At startup the application inverts those
fields into the class-to-SOP and class-to-bucket mappings. Routing policy therefore
lives in the corpus rather than in a duplicate table in application code.

The runtime uses exact lookup instead of vector search. With 17 authored documents
and a closed 10-class taxonomy, the mapping is complete, deterministic, and easy to
audit. A similarity model would add a failure threshold directly before the
escalation decision without solving an ambiguity present in this corpus.

### Holdouts test missing knowledge

Fourteen SOPs are indexed and three are deliberately held out:

- `SOP-INC-001` and `SOP-INC-002` remove all indexed support for
  `rental_income` and `foreign_income_dta`. The router derives
  `no_supporting_sop` from the empty lookup and escalates.
- `SOP-REL-005` removes the overall personal-relief cap from an otherwise
  supported class. This creates a partial-knowledge case without making all tax
  relief questions unanswerable.

The agent never computes a citizen's tax or relief amount. Computation requests are
flagged and escalated because caps, ordering rules, and interacting reliefs cannot be
handled safely from a short prose procedure.

### The SOPs are synthetic

The files are author-written procedures based only on public IRAS guidance. Every
fact in a spec names a source handle, every handle resolves to a URL declared in the
same spec, and every rendered document carries a synthetic banner. Invented queue
names and handling targets are marked as illustrative.

Approved phrasing is rendered into each SOP as grounded source material. Live replies
are still produced only by the configured drafter; the application has no local
template fallback.

## Corpus inventory

| SOP | Intent | Indexed |
|---|---|---:|
| `SOP-FIL-001` | filing | yes |
| `SOP-REL-001` to `SOP-REL-004` | tax_reliefs | yes |
| `SOP-REL-005` | tax_reliefs | no |
| `SOP-ASM-001` | assessment_and_amendment | yes |
| `SOP-PAY-001`, `SOP-PAY-002` | payment | yes |
| `SOP-RES-001` | residency | yes |
| `SOP-ESC-001` | account-specific officer guidance; no class | yes |
| `SOP-ESC-002` | hardship_or_waiver | yes |
| `SOP-ESC-003` | scam_report | yes |
| `SOP-RTE-001`, `SOP-RTE-002` | oos_redirect | yes |
| `SOP-INC-001` | rental_income | no |
| `SOP-INC-002` | foreign_income_dta | no |

## Spec schema

```yaml
sop_id: SOP-PAY-001
title: Handling GIRO enquiries
version: "1.0"
effective_date: 2026-01-01
supersedes: null
applies_to_ya: [2025, 2026]
intents: [payment]           # builds the class-to-SOP mapping
indexed: true                # false keeps the SOP out of runtime lookup
owner_queue: IIT-Payments    # invented, not a real agency queue
handling_target: same_day    # illustrative, not a real SLA
auto_reply_permitted: true
escalate_if:
  - account_specific
  - hardship_or_waiver_request
  - amount_computation_requested

references:
  - id: giro
    url: https://www.iras.gov.sg/...
    fetched: 2026-09-01

scope: >
  What this procedure covers.

not_in_scope:
  - text: The status of a specific taxpayer's GIRO plan.
    route_to: account_specific

facts:
  - text: Deduction date is the 6th of each month.
    source: giro             # must match a references[].id

decision_steps:
  - condition: Asking about a specific failed deduction or amount
    action: Escalate
    reason: account_specific
  - condition: Otherwise
    action: Answer only from the listed facts

approved_phrasing:
  - id: giro_dates
    text: >
      Payments by GIRO are deducted on the 6th of each month.

do_not:
  - Do not confirm whether a specific deduction succeeded or failed.

related: [SOP-PAY-002]
```

## Fields with runtime or build behavior

| Field | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `facts[].source` | Required; generation fails if it does not resolve to a declared reference |
| `indexed: false` | Renders the SOP but excludes it from runtime lookup |
| `intents` | Builds the class-to-SOP mapping |
| `auto_reply_permitted` and `escalate_if` | Determine routing buckets and escalation triggers |
| `approved_phrasing` | Becomes part of the rendered SOP supplied to the drafter |
| `related` | Adds cross-references; one dangling reference is retained deliberately as a missing-knowledge case |

## Validation

```bash
python scripts/generate_sops.py --check
python scripts/derive_taxonomy.py --check
```

The checks reject missing citations, an accidental leak of the held-out relief cap,
held-out classes that have become indexed, and a taxonomy projection that no longer
matches the corpus.

| `data/scenarios/*.yaml` — 116 situations | **Authored by me** | Yes | Original work. |
| `data/generated/emails.jsonl` — 3,000 emails | Generated by GPT-4o from the scenario specs | Yes | Model output; OpenAI grants output rights to the caller. |

| `models/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` | Hugging Face | Yes | Apache 2.0; upstream licence and attribution are included beside the weights. |

---

## 2. The SOP corpus — authored, not scraped

**No agency publishes its internal SOPs.** Any honest version of this project must
author them, and pretending otherwise would be the more serious misrepresentation.

Each of the 17 SOPs is a **synthetic officer-facing procedure**. Every factual claim
in one traces to a public IRAS URL recorded in that file's `references:` frontmatter —
**30 distinct URLs**, all on `www.iras.gov.sg`.

Three structural guarantees, enforced at load time rather than by convention:

- **Every SOP carries a synthetic banner.** `src/triage/sop/loader.py` raises at
  startup if `synthetic: true` is missing. A corpus that could be mistaken for real
  agency material is the failure mode this guards against.
- **Every SOP must declare at least one reference.** An empty `references:` list is a
  hard load error.
- **Citations are checked, not assumed.** `python scripts/generate_sops.py --check`
  validates that all 148 recorded facts resolve to a declared source. It is a
  Makefile target and part of the normal build.

None of these files reflects internal IRAS material, template, or practice. They are
my reconstruction of what such a procedure would plausibly contain. The
[SOP authoring schema](sop_specs/README.md) is the integration point through which a
real agency could provide its own procedures without changing application code.

### 2.1 How the reference pages were used

`scripts/fetch_reference.py` fetches the registry of public pages into `.scratch/`,
which is **gitignored** (`.gitignore` line 3). The manifest records the URL, fetch date
(2026-09-01), HTTP status and byte count for each.

The fetched HTML exists **only** so that facts written into the SOP specs can be
checked against their source during human review. It is never committed, never
redistributed, and never fed to a model.

Politeness measures: a courtesy rate-limit between requests (`--delay`, default
applied in the fetch loop), a single pass rather than a crawl, and a fixed registry of
~30 named pages rather than link-following. A browser User-Agent is set because the
IRAS site serves a JavaScript navigation shell to unknown agents and returns no
content otherwise — this is to receive the page a human would see, not to evade a
restriction.

`https://www.iras.gov.sg/robots.txt` was checked on **2026-09-03** and returned HTTP
404, so there were no published crawler directives to apply. Absence of a robots file
is not treated as permission: the fixed allowlist, one-second delay, single pass, and
Terms-of-Use analysis below still govern the fetch.

### 2.2 Licensing position, stated plainly

IRAS Terms of Use restrict reproduction of site contents. Read literally, they also
require written permission to hyperlink to an internal page — a provision that reads
as boilerplate and is not observed in practice anywhere on the Singapore web.

**This project does not depend on resolving that question**, because it does not
reproduce site content. The operative principle is that **copyright protects
expression, not facts**. A filing deadline, a relief cap, and a penalty rate are facts
stated in or derived from legislation; they are not anyone's creative expression.

What is committed is my own prose restating those facts, with a citation to where each
came from. What is not committed is any IRAS page, in whole or in part.

**Note on figures.** Relief caps and rates in the SOPs are stated as the public pages
state them. They are a snapshot taken 2026-09-01 and will go stale — a production
version would need effective-date metadata and a re-indexing cadence, which is listed
under future improvements in the README.

---

## 3. Synthetic emails

3,000 emails generated by **GPT-4o** from 116 hand-authored scenario specifications.

### 3.1 Why synthetic

Real citizen correspondence to a tax authority contains NRICs, addresses, income
figures and financial distress. It cannot be obtained lawfully for a take-home
exercise, cannot be ethically used if it could, and no public corpus of Singapore
government email enquiries exists. Synthetic is the only honest option here, and the
question becomes whether it is generated well enough to support a claim.

### 3.2 What makes it defensible

**The generator never sees the label.** It receives a *situation* description
("someone received a message claiming to be from the tax authority asking them to
confirm bank details, and wants to know if it is real"). The class label is attached
afterward from the scenario file. The model cannot write toward a class name, which is
the mechanism that would otherwise plant a giveaway token in every email of a class.

**Three independent axes of variation:**

- *Content* — persona, life situation, and the guidance actually relevant to it.
- *Style* — standard English; imperfect English with typos, run-ons and all-caps;
  lightly Singlish-inflected. Register calibrated against sampled real CFPB complaints
  (read for tone; no text copied).
- *Season* — filing period, estimates, notice-of-assessment period.

Plus an edge-case slice: answerable only from held-out guidance, account-specific
phrasing, and genuine edge cases recalled from prior call-centre experience.

**Model separation.** The generator (OpenAI GPT-4o) differs from the zero-shot
classification baseline and the groundedness judge (both Groq/Qwen). No model in the
evaluation path is ever scored on text it wrote — enforced as an explicit rule in
`config/models.yaml`.

### 3.3 Leakage is tested, not assumed

`python scripts/check_leakage.py` runs seven checks over the committed corpus. All
seven pass on the current one:

0. **Balance** — class counts against the taxonomy (300 per class × 10).
1. **Vocabulary leakage** — a TF-IDF + logistic-regression probe. It should classify
   *well but not perfectly*: a near-perfect score means a giveaway token exists and the
   corpus needs regenerating. Measured accuracy sits in the expected band.
2. **System vocabulary** — no email contains the system's own terms (bucket names,
   SOP ids, class names).
3. **Length as a giveaway** — that message length alone does not carry class signal.
4. **Near-duplicates** — cosine similarity across the corpus.
5. **Boilerplate** — that generated openings and closings do not cluster by class.
6. **Flag confounding** — that a lexical flag is not standing in for a class.

Separately, **splits are grouped by `scenario_id`**, so every variant of a situation
lands in the same split and no paraphrase straddles the train/test boundary. That is
enforced in `scripts/make_splits.py` and verified by zero scenario overlap between
every pair of splits.

### 3.4 Privacy in the generated data

- **All identifiers were generated for the project, not sourced from people.** NRICs
  are checksum-valid so the detector can be tested honestly. The values were not
  checked against official registries, so accidental collision cannot be ruled out.
- Addresses combine public Singapore street and estate names with generated block and
  unit numbers. Phone numbers and postal codes are generated in valid-looking shapes.
- No personal identifier belonging to the author or a known person was used.
- **What was planted is recorded** (`plant_pii` per email), which is what makes scrub
  recall measurable rather than asserted.

### 3.5 Privacy in the pipeline itself

Beyond the data, three properties of the system:

- **Scrubbing happens before any external call.** The classifier and the drafter both
  see placeholder text; real values never leave the machine. Rehydration is local and
  happens after the network call, in exactly one place.
- **No PII in committed results.** `eval/metrics/pii_recall.py` masks missed values at
  the point of capture (`S0433218J` → `S0*****8J`), so the module that measures
  containment cannot itself write an identifier into `eval/results/`.
- **`.env` is gitignored** and `triage.env.key_status()` reports only booleans, never
  key values.

---

## 4. CFPB Consumer Complaint Database

- **Source:** [US Consumer Financial Protection Bureau complaint
  database](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/data-research/consumer-complaints/),
  accessed through a Hugging Face copy during style review.
- **Privacy:** CFPB publishes complaint narratives only after removing personal
  information. No narrative is stored or redistributed by this project.
- **Use:** read to calibrate *register* — how members of the public actually write to
  an institution when frustrated, confused, or in financial difficulty. Sentence
  length, politeness markers, how a complaint opens.
- **Not used for:** training, evaluation, or text reuse. No CFPB text appears in this
  repository. It is American and about consumer finance, so it is a style reference
  only, never a content one.

---

## 5. Model weights

- **`sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`** — Apache 2.0, from Hugging Face.
  Committed to the repo (~88 MB fine-tuned) so a clone yields real weights rather than
  git-lfs pointers. The upstream licence and attribution notice are included beside
  both the base encoder and the fine-tuned derivative.
- Gemini, Groq and OpenAI are accessed by API under their respective terms. No weights
  are redistributed.

---

## 6. What this data does not cover

Recorded here as well as in the README, because it bounds every number reported:

- **116 situations is the binding constraint**, not 3,000 emails. Per-class figures
  rest on ~90 test emails drawn from a handful of situations each, so a class can look
  strong because its few situations happen to be easy.
- **A synthetic ceiling.** This measures performance on a distribution GPT-4o and I
  jointly imagined. It cannot tell you a real inbox looks like this — that is the one
  thing this project cannot check about itself.
- **One agency, one tax type.** Individual income tax only. No corporate tax, GST,
  property tax, or stamp duty.
- **English only**, with Singlish inflection. No Chinese, Malay or Tamil.
- **No attachments, no threads, no forwarded chains.** Every email is a single
  standalone message, which real correspondence often is not.
- **Author-shaped distribution.** The scenario set reflects what I judged
  representative. A real inbox would be shaped by seasonality, campaigns, and
  events nobody anticipated.

The most valuable next data step is not more emails — it is **more situations**, and a
validation-only slice of real anonymised enquiries to test whether the synthetic
situation set resembles the real one.
